# 2026-07-15 — Qualified interface identity (v12)

- Added `13_09_qualified_interface_identity`, where a static import of a
  package-local `Display` intentionally collides with kernel `Display`. A
  private `Hidden` implementation returns, casts, passes as a parameter, and
  dispatches through the imported interface, producing `Ada` in tree-walker,
  bytecode, parity, and generated binary runs.
- Interface definitions now carry package-qualified identities. Runtime impl
  lookup and dictionary caches canonicalize through that identity while
  retaining a non-overwriting short-name compatibility alias. The compiler now
  resolves selected static interface imports before global names and emits the
  qualified identity for interface metadata and compiled impl-thunk
  registration. This is a general semantic repair, not a performance path.

# 2026-07-14 — Mutex Await Journal, async liveness, and generic lambda bytecode cache (v12)

- Added the 30th verifier-backed application, `mutex_await_journal`, under
  active v12 examples and the sibling benchmark repository. Four goroutine
  workers use public `Mutex.await_lock` inside ordinary helper calls, update a
  shared named `Journal`, and unlock in `ensure`; Able, Go, Python, and Ruby
  agree on `4:512:2048:1056301196:108896:1056301196`.
- Registered the dedicated `mutex-await-journal` suite, concurrency and
  30-application coverage membership, goroutine/source-root settings, output
  verifier, Docker lanes, comparison mapping, and audit help. The complete
  bytecode audit passes with 130 functions / 7,211 instructions; the compiled
  boundary audit and all three Able modes verify output.
- Repaired generic async correctness in tree-walker, bytecode, and generated
  compiled runtime: mutex await registration is now atomic with its locked
  check, await registrations are cleared and re-armed after every wake,
  blocked state is atomic, and async helper/direct calls preserve the owning
  task payload instead of sharing one VM call stack. Fixed compiler lowering
  of nested `ensure` inside native lambdas. Focused public-await tests pass
  repeatedly; generated and interpreter race checks pass.
- Kept a bounded, binding-shape-aware cache of immutable lambda bytecode
  programs after two independent mutex applications and three unrelated
  bytecode guards supported it. It removes repeated generic closure lowering,
  not a Mutex/container/benchmark-specific path. The controlled bounded lane
  improved Mutex Ledger 4.7%, Await Journal 3.4%, split/join 4.7%, and iterator
  collect 2.6%; numeric Array map was within 2.1% timing noise and reduced its
  allocation count from 329 to 95/op.
- Fresh three-run screens remain a product-status miss, not a reason to
  specialize: bytecode is 5.69x–10.32x Python across the two apps and compiled
  is 180x–205x Go. No `able-stdlib` change was required. Next profile the
  residual Awaitable dispatcher/registration path across Mutex Await Journal,
  Await Channel Mux, and Future Await Race before considering another generic
  runtime change.

# 2026-07-03 — Profile nested match expression bytecode and reject env-aware struct-literal lowering (v12)

- Scope:
  - follow the prior lookup tranche by refreshing broader bytecode workload
    profiles under bounded settings
  - keep the optimization filter strict: no benchmark-specific opcode fusion,
    named-container special casing, or structure-specific compiler lowering
- Findings:
  - `word_count_small` still spends shared time in bytecode call/member
    dispatch, map lookups, and runtime lexical lookup validation
  - `persistent_sorted_set_i32_small` shows a larger wall in
    `runMatchExpression(...)`, where each matched clause body is executed by a
    nested bytecode VM via `evalExpressionBytecodeWithOptions(...)`
  - opcode stats with `ABLE_BYTECODE_STATS=1` showed both generic named
    struct literal paths active in the sorted-set workload:
    - fallback `bytecodeOpStructLiteral`: about `56k` executions
    - `bytecodeOpStructLiteralNamedFast`: about `106k` executions
- Rejected experiment:
  - tried an env-aware expression-lowering cache context so nested match-body
    expressions could seed visible struct definitions and lower nonzero-field
    named struct literals to the existing generic `StructLiteralNamedFast`
    opcode
  - the change correctly moved fallback `StructLiteral` executions to zero and
    raised `StructLiteralNamedFast` to about `171k`, but wall time regressed:
    - before candidate: `persistent_sorted_set_i32_small` around
      `1.93-1.98s`, `36.1MB/op`, `433k allocs/op`
    - with candidate: around `2.18-2.28s`, `54.5MB/op`, `341k allocs/op`
  - the fresh profile showed the tree-walker struct-literal cost was replaced
    by more nested bytecode VM work under `evalExpressionBytecodeWithOptions`;
    the candidate was reverted before handoff
- Outcome:
  - no production code kept from this tranche
  - useful next target is not more env-aware literal lowering by itself; it is
    reducing nested match-body execution overhead, likely by bytecode-lowering
    match clauses more directly or adding a lighter nested-expression path
- Verification:
  - bounded package checks stayed green:
    - `go test ./pkg/runtime`
    - `go test ./pkg/interpreter -run '^$'`
  - after reverting the candidate, bounded `persistent_sorted_set_i32_small`
    returned to the prior range:
    `1982809938 ns/op`, `36103320 B/op`, `433468 allocs/op`
  - bounded lookup-heavy control:
    - `word_count_small`: `1380335345 ns/op`, `54819424 B/op`,
      `649796 allocs/op`

    without explicit type arguments, without a functional-update source, and

    field values by definition order; this is required both for the new lazy

# 2026-07-01 — Reuse non-escaping bytecode block scope environments generically (v12)

- Scope:
  - continue the post-clause-env bytecode allocation follow-up on the shared
    lexical-scope path
  - keep the optimization generic by targeting ordinary runtime block-scope
    lifetime rather than adding any benchmark-shaped opcode, lowering rule,
    or workload-specific fusion
- What changed:
  - profiled the kept tree and confirmed the next remaining generic
    environment-allocation wall was ordinary bytecode `EnterScope`
    allocation in `runResumable(...)`
  - added a conservative lowering-time transient-scope classifier for
    runtime block scopes that:
    - only applies in non-slot bytecode programs
    - only applies to local-binding block scopes with no direct env-defining
      statements
    - rejects blocks containing escaping constructs such as nested function /
      methods / implementation definitions, lambdas, placeholders, iterator
      literals, and spawns
  - extended bytecode `EnterScope` instructions with a transient marker and
    taught the VM to reuse those envs through an interpreter-local pool
  - threaded transient-scope lifetime through every relevant unwind path:
    - explicit `ExitScope`
    - inline return
    - self-fast minimal return
    - error unwind
    - non-yield final cleanup
    - pooled-VM reset
  - tightened self-fast/full call-frame restore so env state returns to the
    caller scope after inline unwinds while trimming transient scope depth
- Outcome:
  - focused bounded coverage stayed green:
    - `env GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecode(Lowering(SkipsEnvScopeForPureIfBlocks|EmitsEnvScopeForIfBlockDeclaration|EmitsRuntimeScopeOnlyForDirectEnvBlockInSlotFunction|KeepsNonTransientEnvScopeForLambdaCaptureBlock)|VM_TransientBlockScope(ReturnCleanup|KeepsEscapingLambdaCapture)|VMFinishMinimalSelfFastReturnRestoresEnvAndReleasesTransientScopes)$' -count=1 -timeout 120s`
    - `env GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM(FinishRunResumableReleasesUnwound(CallFrames|SelfFastCallFrames|MinimalSelfFastCallFrames)|PushSelfFastMinimalCallFrameUsesMinimalStacks|PushCallFrameUsesMinimalSelfFastWithAmbientControlStacks|SelfFastSlot0FrameRestoresCallerSlot|FinishMinimalSelfFastReturnRestoresEnvAndReleasesTransientScopes)$' -count=1 -timeout 120s`
  - bounded bytecode-runtime spot-check:
    - `word_count_small`: `1497946101 ns/op`, `70892744 B/op`,
      `706796 allocs/op`
  - the refreshed bounded alloc-space profile on `word_count_small` confirms
    the generic lexical-scope wall moved:
    - previous kept profile: `runtime.newEnvironmentBase` about `20.50MB`
      flat, with `bytecodeOpEnterScope` / `runtime.NewEnvironment(vm.env)`
      carrying about `17.50MB` cumulative alloc-space in `runResumable(...)`
    - current profile: `runtime.newEnvironmentBase` about `1MB` flat total,
      `runtime.NewEnvironmentWithBindingSets(...)` about `1MB` cumulative,
      and `runResumable(...)` no longer shows `EnterScope` allocation as a
      dominant line
  - the next reusable wall on this workload is now general call/member
    dispatch and shared runtime/struct materialization
    (`execCallOpcode(...)`, `execCallMember(...)`,
    `evaluateStructLiteral(...)`) rather than lexical child-environment

- Next:

    baseline
  - profile the surviving shared dispatch/runtime materialization wall across
    multiple workloads before keeping any further VM changes

# 2026-07-01 — Reuse bytecode call-env caches across equivalent runtime binding sets (v12)

- Scope:
  - follow up on the persistent HAMT helper-call / lookup / env wall that
    remained after the kept canonical array-slot cache reuse tranche
  - stay strictly on the shared call/binding path instead of adding any
    benchmark-shaped lowering or opcode fusion
- What changed:

    environments are keyed by the effective runtime binding set rather than by
    the calling AST node when that binding set is equivalent
  - explicit runtime type bindings now reuse cached envs across different call
    sites when the serialized binding content matches, while call-local method
    binding envs reuse across sites when the function and receiver type match

    explicit binding value cannot be encoded into the generic cache key
  - added focused interpreter coverage for equivalent explicit call sites,
    equivalent call-local call sites, and mixed explicit/call-local cases that
    must stay separated when the binding sets differ

# 2026-06-30 — Keep small fixed-width shift/bitwise execution on the shared integer fast path before `big.Int` fallback (v12)

- Scope:
  - shared tree-walker/bytecode integer bitwise and shift semantics
  - focused regression coverage for small signed/unsigned shift behavior and
    overflow diagnostics
  - bounded benchmark verification against the previously-profiled
    `crc32_small` bitwise workload plus a non-bitwise control
- What changed:
  - updated
    [interpreter_operations_arithmetic.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter_operations_arithmetic.go)
    so `evaluateBitwise(...)` no longer clones `big.Int` operands before it
    knows whether a shared small fixed-width fast path can handle the work
  - added `evaluateSmallIntegerShiftFast(...)` in the same file, covering
    signed and unsigned `<<` / `>>` for fixed-width integer kinds up to
    64 bits while preserving the existing Able semantics:
    - signed right shift stays arithmetic
    - unsigned right shift stays logical
    - left shift still raises `integer overflow` when the result no longer
      fits the destination integer kind
    - out-of-range shift counts still raise `shift out of range`
  - added focused regressions in
    [bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value_test.go)
    and
    [interpreter_numeric_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter_numeric_test.go)
    covering:
    - raw `u32 >> u32`
    - signed `i8 >> i8`
    - signed `i8 << i8`
    - overflowing `u8 << u8`
- Why this keep stayed generic:
  - the change lives in the shared integer operator evaluator reused by both
    interpreters rather than in lowering, opcode selection, or benchmark-only
    runtime branches
  - it extends the existing general small-int bitwise fast path to the
    remaining fixed-width shift cases instead of inventing a workload-shaped
    fused operator
  - the control benchmark check was used to confirm the keep behaves like a
    general operator-path improvement rather than a `crc32_small` trick
- Verification:
  - focused regression slice under `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1`:

  - bounded bytecode-runtime spot-checks under the same memory caps:

    - `word_count_small`: `1555656612 ns/op`, `104150112 B/op`,
      `1031239 allocs/op`
- Outcome:

# 2026-06-29 — slot-lower zero-field struct match patterns when semantics match typed patterns (v12)

- Scope:
  - bytecode slot-lowered `match` clause planning
  - zero-field type-only struct patterns in guardless match clauses
  - regression coverage for the semantic boundaries of that lowering
- What changed:
  - extended
    [bytecodeSlotMatchClausePlanForPattern(...)](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_lowering_match.go:103)
    and
    [bytecodeCanLowerSlotMatchPatternInEnv(...)](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_lowering_match.go:161)
    in
    [bytecode_lowering_match.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_lowering_match.go)
    so guardless zero-field `StructPattern`s can lower through the existing
    typed-pattern slot path when, and only when, that preserves semantics
  - added the new helpers around
    [bytecodeSlotMatchZeroFieldStructPatternTypeExprInContext(...)](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_lowering_match.go:196)
    to keep the rule conservative:
    - allow `IteratorEnd {}` because the runtime already treats it as a
      language-level singleton sentinel outside ordinary struct instances
    - allow known nominal struct definitions only when a zero-field struct
      pattern is semantically equivalent to a typed match
    - reject singleton and non-struct lookalikes so they stay on the generic
      matcher
  - added focused coverage in
    [bytecode_vm_match_slot_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_match_slot_test.go)
    for:
    - positive slot lowering of zero-field named-field struct matches
      ([TestBytecodeVM_SlotLoweringEmitsZeroFieldNamedStructMatchWithoutGenericMatch](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_match_slot_test.go:83))
    - positive slot lowering of runtime `IteratorEnd {}`
      ([TestBytecodeVM_SlotLoweringEmitsIteratorEndStructPatternWithoutGenericMatch](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_match_slot_test.go:121))
    - negative guards that keep zero-field singleton and non-struct patterns on
      generic `Match`
      ([TestBytecodeVM_SlotLoweringZeroFieldSingletonStructPatternFallsBackToGenericMatch](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_match_slot_test.go:244),
      [TestBytecodeVM_SlotLoweringZeroFieldNonStructPatternFallsBackToGenericMatch](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_match_slot_test.go:270))
- Why this keep stayed generic:
  - it does not add a benchmark-only opcode or fuse a benchmark-specific
    expression stencil; it broadens an existing shared lowering route for a
    common language shape: guardless type-only match clauses
  - the conservative def-kind checks are there specifically to avoid the kind
    of benchmark-shaped semantic drift we do not want; singleton structs and
    non-struct names remain on the generic matcher because their behavior is
    not equivalent to typed matching
  - `IteratorEnd` is treated here only as an existing language/runtime special
    type, not as a benchmark name; the same handling applies anywhere the
    runtime iterator sentinel appears
- Verification:
  - focused slot-match regression slice under
    `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1`:
    - `go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_SlotLowering(EmitsTypedPrimitiveMatchOpcode|EmitsTypedNominalMatchOpcode|EmitsZeroFieldNamedStructMatchWithoutGenericMatch|EmitsIteratorEndStructPatternWithoutGenericMatch|EmitsIdentifierBindingMatchWithoutGenericMatch|SingletonIdentifierPatternFallsBackToGenericMatch|TypedSingletonIdentifierPatternFallsBackToGenericMatch|ZeroFieldSingletonStructPatternFallsBackToGenericMatch|ZeroFieldNonStructPatternFallsBackToGenericMatch|TypedNominalMatchWithFields)' -count=1 -timeout 60s`
    - result: `ok able/interpreter-go/pkg/interpreter 0.068s`
  - focused surrounding match/pattern slice:

    - result: `ok able/interpreter-go/pkg/interpreter 0.066s`
  - same-session bounded A/B on the generic iterator-style corpus fixture:
    - kept tree `iterator_match_identifier_small`:
      `34579177 ns/op`, `6415751 B/op`, `81458 allocs/op`
    - temporary reverted baseline in the same session:
      `47289807 ns/op`, `9232990 B/op`, `113348 allocs/op`
  - broad current-tree control spot-check:
    - `word_count_small`: `1499555381 ns/op`, `108925392 B/op`,

- Outcome:
  - kept

  - dead-binding elision for pattern-bound names that clause guard/body never

    keyed by shared `*ast.MatchClause`, so the runtime caches three generic

    with `expressionCurrentScopeBindingCapacity(...)` plus

    so `matchPatternForClause(...)` takes the cached plan, keeps dead pattern

# 2026-06-27 — kept reusable slot-call type-binding envs generic in shared bytecode invocation (v12)

- Scope:
  - shared `invokeFunction(...)` bytecode call setup
  - shared explicit / receiver-derived type-binding env reuse
  - no benchmark-shaped opcode, lowering rule, or named-stdlib special case
- What changed:
  - factored receiver-derived call-local type bindings into a shared
    `callLocalTypeBindingValuesIfAny(...)` helper so the runtime bindings can
    be cached and reused without re-deriving them on every bytecode call
  - extended reusable slot-call env caching from explicit generic call-site
    bindings to the combined explicit-plus-receiver-derived binding case,
    keyed by `(function, call site, receiver type)` when receiver-driven
    bindings are present
  - guarded that reuse with a shared binding-name mutation scan so the cache is
    only used when the callee body cannot reassign synthetic bindings like
    `T`, `T_type`, `Self`, or `Self_type`
  - updated `invokeFunction(...)` to compute the receiver once, reuse the
    cached binding env when eligible, and skip the per-call
    `bindCallLocalTypeBindings(...)` writeback in those reusable cases
- Why this keep stayed generic:

    specializing any benchmark, container, or stdlib nominal type
  - the reuse rule is semantic: it applies whenever slot-lowered bytecode
    calls only need stable synthetic type bindings and the callee cannot
    mutate them
- Verification:
  - focused call/env + member-dispatch regression slice:
    - `env GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestReusableBytecodeCallEnv|TestInvokeFunctionReusesCachedBytecodeCallEnv|TestBytecodeVM_(CallMember|MemberMethodCache)|TestBytecodeTrace' -count=1`

# 2026-06-24 — Matrix regression after matrix-only backouts traced to a generic mirrored-division lowering bug (v12)

- Continued the anti-benchmark-specific cleanup by keeping the recent
  matrix-only lowering/opcode backouts in place and then tracing the remaining
  `matrixmultiply_f64_small` bytecode regression with focused parity tests.
- The new `bytecode_vm_matrix_regression_test.go` isolation cases narrowed the
  wrong result to `build_matrix(...)`: the returned nested rows were
  preserving shape but using `t = 1.0` instead of
  `t = 1.0 / (n as f64) / (n as f64)`.
- Root cause:
  - `bytecodeBinaryCastSlotFloatConstInstructionForOperator(...)` was
    incorrectly accepting both operand orders for `/`
  - that let `1.0 / (n as f64)` lower into the existing
    `BinaryCastSlotFloatConstDiv` fast path as though it were
    `(n as f64) / 1.0`
  - in `build_matrix(...)`, the left-associated scale expression therefore
    became `((n as f64) / 1.0) / (n as f64)`, collapsing `t` to `1.0`
- Fix landed:
  - the cast-slot-float-const lowering now only recognizes the operand order
    actually implemented by the opcode: `(slot as f64) / const`
  - mirrored `const / (slot as f64)` shapes now stay on generic lowering
  - added focused guardrail coverage in
    `bytecode_vm_cast_slot_float_div_test.go` for both the direct expression
    and store-to-slot mirrored cases, plus a function-parameter parity case
  - the matrix regression file kept the broader nested-array parity tests so
    this class of bug still gets caught at workload level
- Focused verification:
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOMAXPROCS=2 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_(LoweringSkipsMirroredBinaryCastSlotFloatConstDivOpcode|LoweringSkipsMirroredStoreSlotCastSlotFloatConstDivOpcode|FunctionParamMirroredFloatDivParity|BuildMatrixSmallParity|BuildMatrixReturnedNestedArrayParity|MatmulSmallParity)' -count=1`
  - result: `ok`
- Bounded benchmark checks:
  - direct bytecode `./v12/ablebc v12/fixtures/bench/matrixmultiply_f64_small/main.able`
    now returns the kept value `-28.500833332098754` instead of the prior huge
    nonsense result
  - `./v12/bench_fixture_validate --benchmarks matrixmultiply_f64_small,mandelbrot_small,automata_dfa_small --modes compiled,bytecode --timeout 20 --build-timeout 120 --go-mem-limit 1GiB --go-gc 50`
  - kept outcomes:
    - `matrixmultiply_f64_small`: compiled/bytecode agree on
      `-28.500833332098754`
    - `mandelbrot_small`: compiled/bytecode remain parity-partial with matching
      hashed output under the bounded harness
    - `automata_dfa_small`: compiled still finishes, bytecode still times out;
      no new semantic mismatch was introduced there
- Follow-on note:
  - this was the exact kind of generally-applicable bug the broadened corpus is
    meant to expose
  - the next bytecode tranche should continue removing single-benchmark
    lowerings/opcodes and then use bounded fixture sweeps to find the next
    recurring generic hotspot or correctness gap

# 2026-06-24 — Inherited-interface lookup no longer duplicates a single impl into an ambiguity (v12)

- Closed the adjacent interpreter correctness bug that was surfacing as
  `ambiguous implementations of Ord for Box: impl Ord for Box` in
  `14_01_operator_interfaces_arithmetic_comparison`.
- Root cause:
  - interface method lookup expands the requested interface through its base
    interfaces so inherited defaults/signatures can resolve
  - for a direct impl like `impl Ord for Box`, the same impl candidate was
    being collected once from `Ord` and again from inherited `PartialOrd`
    search, then carried unchanged into method selection
  - method selection treated those duplicated identical candidates as an
    ambiguity even though there was only one real impl
- Landed change:
  - `v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/impl_resolution.go` now defines
    stable impl-candidate identity keys plus dedupe helpers
  - `v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter_interface_lookup.go`
    now deduplicates impl candidates and method matches before overload /
    ambiguity selection
- Added focused regression:
  - `v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/stdlib_interface_exec_regression_test.go`
    now covers a reduced `impl Ord for Box` comparison shape in both
    treewalker and bytecode modes
- Bounded validation:
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestOrdImplComparisonDoesNotDuplicateCandidatesAcrossInheritedLookup$' -count=1`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestExecFixtures/14_01_operator_interfaces_arithmetic_comparison$' -count=1`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/interpreter -exec-mode bytecode -run 'TestExecFixtures/14_01_operator_interfaces_arithmetic_comparison$' -count=1`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestExecFixtures/(06_12_05_stdlib_numbers_biguint|14_01_operator_interfaces_arithmetic_comparison)$' -count=1`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/interpreter -exec-mode bytecode -run 'TestExecFixtures/(06_12_05_stdlib_numbers_biguint|14_01_operator_interfaces_arithmetic_comparison)$' -count=1`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/compiler -run 'TestCompilerExecFixtures/(06_12_05_stdlib_numbers_biguint|14_01_operator_interfaces_arithmetic_comparison)$' -count=1`
- Follow-on note:
  - with the `BigUint` impl-forwarding recursion and this inherited-interface
    duplication both closed, the next tranche should move back to doubling the
    benchmark corpus and using that broader suite to find the next generic
    compiler / VM / interpreter hotspots

# 2026-06-24 — Impl-body member dispatch now prefers inherent methods over recursive same-name impl forwarding (v12)

- Closed the broader stdlib numeric runtime failure behind
  `TestExecFixtures/06_12_05_stdlib_numbers_biguint` with a generic
  interpreter dispatch fix rather than any `BigUint`-specific special case.
- Root cause:
  - inside an impl/default method body, plain member syntax like
    `self.add(rhs)` was re-entering the current impl method before checking
    whether the concrete receiver type also had an inherent `add` method
  - `BigUint` forwards `Add`/`Sub`/`Mul` impl methods to inherent methods of
    the same name, so the old order recursively re-entered the impl body until
    stack overflow
- Landed change:
  - `v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter_method_resolution.go`
    now prefers an inherent same-name method on the concrete receiver before
    falling back to the current impl-context method set for plain member
    access; impl-context dispatch remains in place for default-method chaining
    and interface-local disambiguation when no inherent method exists
- Added focused regression:
  - `v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/stdlib_interface_exec_regression_test.go`
    now covers an `impl Add ... { self.add(rhs) }` forwarder shape in both
    treewalker and bytecode modes
- Bounded validation:
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestImplMethodForwarderPrefersInherentMethodOnSameConcreteReceiver$' -count=1`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestExecFixtures/(06_12_05_stdlib_numbers_biguint|10_07_interface_default_chain|10_09_interface_named_impl_inherent)$' -count=1`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/interpreter -exec-mode bytecode -run 'TestExecFixtures/(06_12_05_stdlib_numbers_biguint|10_07_interface_default_chain|10_09_interface_named_impl_inherent)$' -count=1`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && GOMAXPROCS=2 GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test ./pkg/compiler -run 'TestCompilerExecFixtures/06_12_05_stdlib_numbers_biguint$' -count=1`
  - `./v12/bench_fixture_validate --benchmarks biguint_add_mul_small --timeout 30 --build-timeout 180 --go-mem-limit 1GiB --go-gc 50`
- Follow-on note:
  - one broader smoke command that also included
    `14_01_operator_interfaces_arithmetic_comparison` currently reports an
    adjacent `Ord for Box` ambiguity in the dirty worktree; that was not part
    of this fix and needs a separate look before treating that fixture as a
    tranche gate

  review because it fused one six-statement Mandelbrot stencil into a bespoke
  opcode.
- That optimization did not key off benchmark names or source paths, but it
  was still too workload-shaped to meet the project bar for generally
  applicable compiler / VM work.
- The smaller prior structural work remains in tree for now; it needs a proper
  cross-benchmark audit instead of a blunt revert based on one case.
- Next acceptance criteria:
  - no benchmark-name or source-path specialization
  - no bespoke long-stencil opcodes for a single benchmark recurrence
  - new fusions must demonstrate reuse across multiple benchmark families or
    clearly improve a broad opcode/value-representation mechanism

# 2026-06-23 — Speculative post-guard float update pair kept the next `mandelbrot` tranche (v12)

- Kept the next pinned `mandelbrot` tranche on the remaining post-guard float
  update boundary instead of broadening helper-local float rewrites again.
- The landed change adds a speculative block-local fast path for the exact
  pair of discarded float assignments that dominate the inner recurrence after
  the escape check:
  - `zi = 2.0 * zr * zi + ci`
  - `zr = zr2 - zi2 + cr`
- Lowering now emits a `bytecodeOpTryFloatUpdatePair` opcode before the normal
  lowered `StoreSlotFloatAddMulSlot` / `StoreSlotFloatAddSub` statements.
  Generic fallback stays in place. The fast path only fires when:
  - both statements are plain `=` assignments
  - the first statement lowers to the existing slot-backed fused
    float-add-mul update with a slot-const multiply stack operand
  - the second statement lowers to the existing fused float add-sub update
  - the second RHS does not read the first target slot
- On success the VM reads all source slots first, computes both raw float
  results, writes both discarded slot updates directly, and jumps over the
  generic fallback statements.
- Focused verification:
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_(LoweringEmitsTryFloatUpdatePair|LoweringSkipsTryFloatUpdatePairWhenSecondUpdateReadsFirstTarget|TryFloatUpdatePairFastPath|TryFloatUpdatePairParity|LoweringEmitsFloatMulAddMulCompareConstJumpWithTempStores|FloatMulAddMulCompareConstJumpTempStoreParity|FloatAddSubSlotUpdateParity|StoreSlotFloatAddMulSlotFastPath)$'`
  - `./v12/bench_perf --cpu-affinity 2-3 --runs 1 --timeout 60 --modes bytecode-runtime --run-from ../benchmarks v12/examples/benchmarks/mandelbrot/mandelbrot.able`
  - `./v12/bench_compare_external --cpu-affinity 2-3 --benchmarks mandelbrot,matrixmultiply --modes bytecode --runs 3 --timeout 60`
  - repeat external confirmation with the same pinned settings
- Kept measurements:
  - pinned runtime `mandelbrot`:
    - `4475508943 ns/op`, `330949352 B/op`, `34613552 allocs/op`
  - first cached-stdlib external confirmation (`3/3`):
    - `mandelbrot`: `4.7633s`
    - `matrixmultiply`: `0.5367s`
  - repeated cached-stdlib external confirmation (`3/3`):
    - `mandelbrot`: `4.4233s`
    - `matrixmultiply`: `0.5433s`
  - kept post-tranche profile (`ABLE_GO_CPU_PROFILE` with preserved workdir):
    - hottest residual lanes are now
      `execJumpIfFloatMulAddMulCompareConstFalse(...)`,
      `execTryFloatUpdatePair(...)`,
      `storeReusableNormalizedFloatSlotRawDiscard(...)`, and
      `execStoreSlotBinaryIntSlotConstDiscardI32Fast(...)`
- Outcome:
  - keep the speculative post-guard float update pair
  - the next productive tranche should re-profile from this new baseline and
    stay structural, likely targeting the remaining compare/store + `iter += 1`
    discard traffic around the same inner recurrence rather than reopening the
    rejected broader `f64` lane or whole-loop kernel rewrites

# 2026-06-23 — Structural temp-square compare/store fusion kept the next `mandelbrot` tranche (v12)

- Took the next pinned `mandelbrot` tranche as a structural lowering cut
  instead of another generic float-helper rewrite.
- The landed change reuses the existing
  `bytecodeOpJumpIfFloatMulAddMulCompareConstFalse` opcode for the exact local
  sequence:
  - `zr2 := zr * zr`
  - `zi2 := zi * zi`
  - `if zr2 + zi2 > 4.0 { ... }`
- The match is intentionally narrow:
  - both square statements must be simple declarations
  - the `if` must have no `else` / `elsif`
  - the `if` body must terminate control flow
  - the `if` body must not reference `zr2` / `zi2`
  - later statements in the block must reference those temp names
- Lowering now declares the temp slots, emits the existing fused compare jump
  with per-site target-slot metadata, and skips the two standalone
  `StoreSlotFloatBinary` square stores.
- The VM computes the two products once, evaluates the compare, and only
  materializes `zr2` / `zi2` into their temp slots on the false path where the
  loop continues and later statements still need them.
- Focused verification:
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_(LoweringEmitsFloatMulAddMulCompareConstJump|LoweringEmitsFloatMulAddMulCompareConstJumpWithTempStores|LoweringKeepsFloatBinaryStoresWhenIfBodyUsesTempSquares|FloatMulAddMulCompareConstJumpParity|FloatMulAddMulCompareConstJumpTempStoreParity|FloatMulAddMulCompareConstJumpFastPathWithOwnedFloatSlots|FloatMulAddMulCompareConstJumpStoresTempSquaresOnFalsePath|FloatAddSubSlotUpdateParity|StoreSlotFloatAddMulSlotFastPath|FloatBinaryStoreDiscardResultKeepsSnapshotSemantics)$'`
  - `./v12/bench_perf --cpu-affinity 2-3 --runs 1 --timeout 60 --modes bytecode-runtime --run-from ../benchmarks v12/examples/benchmarks/mandelbrot/mandelbrot.able`
  - `./v12/bench_compare_external --cpu-affinity 2-3 --benchmarks mandelbrot,matrixmultiply --modes bytecode --runs 3 --timeout 60`
- Kept measurements:
  - pinned runtime `mandelbrot`:
    - `4947703038 ns/op`, `450787976 B/op`, `49593354 allocs/op`
  - first cached-stdlib external confirmation (`3/3`):
    - `mandelbrot`: `5.5533s`
    - `matrixmultiply`: `0.5700s`
  - repeated cached-stdlib external confirmation (`3/3`):
    - `mandelbrot`: `5.1000s`
    - `matrixmultiply`: `0.5233s`
- Outcome:
  - keep the structural temp-square compare/store fusion
  - do not reopen the rejected broader `f64` lane or same-slot square
    micro-path; this win came from changing the local control-flow shape
  - the next productive tranche should stay on that same structural strategy
    and target the remaining post-guard Mandelbrot recurrence update chain
    rather than another generic helper-local float rewrite

# 2026-06-20 — fused coordinate-affine float store kept the next `mandelbrot` tranche (v12)

- Kept the next `mandelbrot` float tranche on the exact remaining coordinate
  affine setup instead of keeping the narrower cast-slot multiply probe that
  had regressed the real workload.
- The landed change is deliberately shaped around the benchmarked hot path:
  - removed the failed `bytecodeOpBinaryCastSlotFloatConstMul` experiment
  - lowering now emits `bytecodeOpStoreSlotFloatAffine` for
    `((scale * (slot as f64)) / (name as f64)) - offset` assignment shapes
    such as:
    - `ci := ((2.0 * (y as f64)) / (SIZE as f64)) - 1.0`
    - `cr := ((2.0 * (x as f64)) / (SIZE as f64)) - 1.5`
  - the VM uses an IP-keyed affine plan carrying the source slot, divisor slot
    or name, target float kind, scale, and offset, then evaluates the whole
    multiply/divide/subtract chain through the raw-float fast path before the
    final store
- Focused verification:
  - `go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_(LoweringEmitsStoreSlotFloatAffine|StoreSlotFloatAffineParity|StoreSlotFloatAffineFastPathUsesI32RegisterLaneAndGlobalDivisor|LoweringEmitsBinaryCastSlotFloatConstDivOpcode|BinaryCastSlotFloatConstDivParity|BinaryCastSlotFloatConstDivFastPathUsesI32RegisterLane|LoweringEmitsStoreSlotCastSlotFloatConstDivOpcode|StoreSlotCastSlotFloatConstDivParity|StoreSlotCastSlotFloatConstDivFastPathUsesI32RegisterLane|StoreSlotCastSlotFloatConstDivDiscardFastPathStoresRawFloatWithoutOwnedCell|StoreSlotCastSlotFloatConstDivDiscardFastPathUpdatesExistingOwnedSlotCellWithoutMap|StoreSlotCastSlotFloatConstDivDiscardFastPathUsesRawI64SourceAndExistingOwnedTarget|LoweringEmitsBinaryFloatMulSlotConst|LoweringUsesBinaryFloatMulSlotConstInsideFloatAddMulUpdate|BinaryFloatMulSlotConstFastPath|BinaryFloatMulSlotConstParity|LoweringEmitsFloatBinaryStore|FloatBinaryStoreParity|FloatBinaryStoreDiscardResultKeepsSnapshotSemantics|LoweringEmitsFloatAddSubStore|FloatAddSubParity|LoweringEmitsFloatAddMulSlotUpdateWithNonTargetBase|FloatAddMulNonTargetBaseParity)' -count=1`
  - `./v12/bench_perf --runs 1 --timeout 120 --modes bytecode-runtime --run-from ../benchmarks v12/examples/benchmarks/mandelbrot/mandelbrot.able`
  - `./v12/bench_compare_external --benchmarks mandelbrot,matrixmultiply --modes bytecode --runs 3 --timeout 60`
  - `./v12/bench_compare_external --benchmarks mandelbrot --modes bytecode --runs 5 --timeout 60`
- Kept measurements:
  - runtime `mandelbrot` confirmation:
    `6279413279 ns/op`, `596996648 B/op`, `66588389 allocs/op`
  - cached-stdlib external bytecode `mandelbrot` improved to `6.4040s` over
    `5/5` (the first `3/3` read of `6.6967s` was noise-sized and not the kept
    number)
  - cached-stdlib external bytecode `matrixmultiply` improved to `0.5167s`

- The useful conclusion is specific: the remaining `mandelbrot` coordinate
  affine setup was still large enough that the right store-shaped fusion beats
  another isolated binary opcode. The next productive float tranche should
  re-profile from this new baseline and likely target the remaining slot-load /
  name-lookup / float-store boundaries inside `pixel_byte`, not reopen the
  isolated cast-slot multiply probe or broader raw-float representation
  experiments.

    write directly into an existing owned float slot cell when one is already
    present

    `StoreSlotCastSlotFloatConstDiv`
  - backed the same reuse out of plain `StoreSlotFloatBinary` and plain
    `StoreSlotFloatAddMul` after profiling showed those lanes shifting
    allocation into `bytecodeStackSnapshotValue(...)` and regressing runtime
    `mandelbrot`
  - added focused owned-cell reuse allocation coverage for the cast-slot path

  - `go test ./pkg/interpreter -count=1 -timeout 300s` still fails only on the

    `mandelbrot` to `8563048519 ns/op`, `1166922760 B/op`,

  - `bytecodeDirectFloatCompareFast(...)` and a raw helper now compare

    directly
  - `execBinary(...)` now uses that path before materializing through the
    generic fast/fallback operator ladder
  - `compareBytecodeCondition(...)` now uses the same direct float compare path
    before falling through to generic operator handling
- Focused verification:
  - direct float compare fast-path unit coverage
  - direct float compare parity coverage
  - existing float arithmetic/store/jump parity coverage
- Kept measurements:
  - runtime `mandelbrot` moved from the restored post-backout control
    `12783506275 ns/op`, `2783102432 B/op`, `300798658 allocs/op`
    to `10834374807 ns/op`, `2398954784 B/op`, `284792308 allocs/op`
  - cached-stdlib external bytecode `mandelbrot` moved from `13.2300s`
    to `11.2100s`
  - cached-stdlib external bytecode `matrixmultiply` stayed in the same
    general band at `0.5400s`
- The useful conclusion is specific: a local boundary cut around raw-float
  comparison does pay off, unlike the broader slot/stack sidecar probes.
  The next `mandelbrot` tranche should stay on this same condition path and
  try to eliminate the remaining bool stack round-trip, likely with a direct
  float-add-compare-const jump for the `zr2 + zi2 > 4.0` escape test.

# 2026-06-20 — rejected stack-local float-cell follow-up and restored control (v12)

- Followed the rejected slot-only sidecar with a narrower stack/register probe
  aimed directly at the `mandelbrot` hot stack path, then measured it instead
  of assuming the lower allocation count would translate into a real keep.
- The first active variant used pooled stack-local `*runtime.FloatValue` cells
  for float loads/results plus explicit call-boundary materialization. It
  cut the direct runtime band to `1834321752 B/op`, `78319459 allocs/op`, but
  it was not a keep:
  - cached-stdlib external `mandelbrot` regressed to `28.2600s`
  - cached-stdlib external `matrixmultiply` landed at `0.5500s`
  - the direct runtime confirmation regressed to `28454783500 ns/op`
- A lighter follow-up that backed out the pooled cell path but kept the
  stack-side float normalization helpers still did not hold:
  - cached-stdlib external `mandelbrot` regressed to `17.6200s`
  - cached-stdlib external `matrixmultiply` held near the old band at
    `0.5200s`
  - the direct runtime confirmation landed at `16682311702 ns/op`,
    `3131617712 B/op`, `346922621 allocs/op`
- Backed the active stack-side probe out of the hot path and re-confirmed the
  control:
  - `mandelbrot` runtime spot check restored to
    `12783506275 ns/op`, `2783102432 B/op`, `300798658 allocs/op`
  - cached-stdlib external `mandelbrot` restored to `13.2300s`
  - cached-stdlib external `matrixmultiply` re-confirmed in the same general
    band at `0.7800s` on a follow-up one-shot
- The useful conclusion is specific: reducing float alloc counts by routing the
  VM stack through pooled `*runtime.FloatValue` cells, or by more aggressively
  normalizing float loads/results into fresh raw carriers, is still slower than
  the kept raw-float-carrier baseline. The next credible `mandelbrot` cut
  needs a true raw stack/register sidecar or a more local removal of
  `bytecodeRawFloatSlotValue(...)` / `bytecodeMaterializeRawFloatValue(...)`
  cost without introducing pointer/pool bookkeeping into the hot float loop.

# 2026-06-19 — `mandelbrot` raw-float slot lane kept another bytecode cut (v12)

- Added a bounded raw-float carrier layer inside the bytecode VM:
  - `bytecodeRawF32SlotValue`
  - `bytecodeRawF64SlotValue`
- Wired the hot float path to keep those carriers unboxed across:
  - direct float binary arithmetic

  - slot loads onto the VM stack

    float-specialized path

    call handling

  - inline return, direct return, and VM exit materialize before values leave
    the bytecode VM

  value semantics rather than concrete `runtime.FloatValue` storage shape.

    came from `ABLE_PATH` source-resolution overhead and is not the comparable

# 2026-06-17 — Dormant value-slot sidecar regression traced to affine temp boxing; control restored (v12)

- Kept the value-slot `i32` sidecar substrate dormant, but fixed the
  substrate-only quicksort prefix regression in
  [v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_int_affine_update.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_int_affine_update.go).
- Root cause: `StoreSlotIntMulConstAddFromSlot` stopped reusing a non-nil slot
  payload and started synthesizing a temporary raw `runtime.Value` for the
  parser hot path even when `vm.slots[target]` already held the current value.
  On the external quicksort parser loop (`value = value * 10 + digit`) that
  reintroduced out-of-cache `i32` boxing/allocation churn and made the
  dormant-sidecar tree look slower than the real pre-sidecar control.
- The fix is narrow: when the source slot already has a concrete value, reuse
  it directly; only fall back to raw register/value-slot materialization when
  the slot is actually nil-backed.
- Measurements on the 1 MB external-style prefix after the fix:
  - `go test` runtime bench (`count=3`, `benchtime=1x`):
    `797003542 ns/op`, `21586416 B/op`, `500078 allocs/op`
    `797798779 ns/op`, `21586448 B/op`, `500080 allocs/op`
    `820190253 ns/op`, `21586416 B/op`, `500078 allocs/op`
  - `bench_perf` (`runs=3`):
    `801039889 ns/op`, `21586315 B/op`, `500077 allocs/op`
- Reduced quicksort hotloop stayed in the current band at
  `5954419-7294060 ns/op` over `100x`; this tranche is about restoring the
  parser/control baseline, not a new partition-loop keep.
- Verification:

  - external-style `bench_perf`:

# 2026-06-17 — Generic Int fib recurrence now preserves exact result kinds across widening (v12)

- Kept the next recurrence-policy slice across
  [v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence.go),
  [v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_generic.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_generic.go),
  [v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_test.go),
  and
  [v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_generic_int_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_generic_int_test.go).
- Before this slice, the generic-`Int` recurrence path still had a real
  semantic gap even after the earlier source-shape keeps: the native kernel
  only tracked one execution kind, while tree-walker generic `Int` recurrence
  can change both recursive argument kinds and result kinds as integer
  promotion proceeds. The old parity checks only compared numeric equality, so
  cases like `if n <= 2_i64 { return 1 }`, `if n <= 2_i64 { return 1_i32 }`,
  and `if n <= 1 { return n }` on live `u64` input could hide wrong integer
  suffixes even when the numeric value matched.
- The keep now matches the real arithmetic semantics instead of relying on a
  one-kind shortcut:
  - generic-`Int` recurrence execution now evaluates per-state `(n, kind)`
    pairs and memoizes the exact result kind/value for each state when it
    genuinely needs a multi-kind state space
  - recursive subtraction uses the same `promoteIntegerTypes(...)` rules as the
    normal interpreter, so widening states like live `u64` plus untyped `1`/`2`
    offsets now run natively instead of taking one boxed step first
  - base returns preserve their real runtime kinds, so constant-base `i64`
    source like `if n <= 2_i64 { return 1 }` now returns `i32` at both base and
    non-base points, while mixed current/constant seeds still widen exactly
    where tree-walker does
  - common cases where every recursive child stabilizes to one widened kind
    after the first subtraction now fold back to a dense DP table keyed by raw
    `n`, so the exact-kind keep no longer has to pay the full `(raw, kind)` map
    cost on straight-line generic fib shapes
  - the remaining true multi-kind nonnegative fallback now tracks only the
    reachable `(raw, kind)` frontier for the root entry, replacing the old
    hash-map memo with indexed slice state for mixed recursive-kind sources
  - oversize nonnegative generic-`Int` recurrence no longer drops to that
    fallback immediately: when the indexed DP tables still fit under a bounded
    byte budget, the runtime keeps the oversize source on the adaptive dense DP
    lane and, once the estimated table exceeds that budget, switches to a paged
    indexed DP layout before falling all the way back to the sparse raw-row
    memo; that memo path now pre-indexes stride-aligned nonnegative states
    directly, using a flat row table while it fits and paged on-grid rows
    before leaving the spill map only for off-grid cases, and the paged DP
    gate now also recognizes close-step semigroup density so sources like
    `1000/1001` can bypass the stack memo entirely; the density cutoff is now
    explicit and calibrated at the 50% reachable-row boundary after direct
    strategy comparisons around the `1049/1051` crossover
- Added focused coverage for:
  - generic `Int` `i64` untyped const-range / `<` parity now asserting `i32`
    results explicitly
  - generic `Int` `i64` explicit-`i32` const-range base/non-base parity as
    `i32`
  - generic `Int` `i64` explicit-`i32` mixed-seed base/non-base parity split
    across `i32` and `i64`
  - generic `Int` `i32` mixed recursive-kind source
    `if n <= 1 { return n } fib(n - 1_i64) + fib(n - 2)` now asserting `i32`
    base cases, `i64` non-base results, and direct fast-path success
  - oversize generic `Int` `i32` mixed recursive-kind zero source
    `if n <= 2_i64 { return 0 } fib(n - 1_i64) + fib(n - 2)` now asserting
    direct fast-path success above `bytecodeI32RecurrenceDPMaxInput`
  - generic `Int` `i32` three-kind recursive source
    `if n <= 2_i64 { return 0 } fib(n - 1_i64) + fib(n - 2_i128)` now
    asserting parity on the small source plus direct fast-path success on the
    oversize source that stays above the dense-DP byte budget
  - generic `Int` `i32` sparse three-kind recursive source
    `if n <= 2000_i64 { return 0 } fib(n - 1000_i64) + fib(n - 2000_i128)` now
    asserting detection, small parity, and direct fast-path success on the
    oversize sparse source that stays behind the paged lane
  - generic `Int` `i32` spill-heavy three-kind recursive source
    `if n <= 2000_i64 { return 0 } fib(n - 1000_i64) + fib(n - 1001_i128)` now
    asserting detection, small parity, and direct fast-path success on the
    close-step source that misses the flat stride budget
  - generic `Int` `u64` untyped current-return direct fast-path success plus
    base-case `u64` vs non-base `i128` parity
- Measured on temporary generic-`Int` recurrence probes:
  - pre-fix steady-state bytecode-runtime probe:
    - untyped current-return `fib(40_u64)`: `0.1500s` over `3/3`
  - exact-kind follow-up with stable-recursive-kind DP recovery:
    - untyped current-return `fib(40_u64)`: stayed in the `0.1300s` over `3/3`
      band while dropping from `25000 B/op, 44 allocs/op` to
      `20032 B/op, 38 allocs/op`
    - explicit-`i32` const-range `fib(40_i64)`: `ns/op=42260`,
      `20032 B/op`, `38 allocs/op`
    - untyped const-range `fib(40_i64)`: `ns/op=53583`, `20032 B/op`,
      `38 allocs/op`
  - true multi-kind nonnegative fallback recovery:
    - mixed recursive-kind `fib(30_i32)` moved from `0.1300s` over `3/3`,
      `25048 B/op`, `45 allocs/op` to `0.1167s` over `3/3`, `20768 B/op`,
      `43 allocs/op`
  - oversize adaptive dense-DP recovery:
    - mixed recursive-kind zero source
      `if n <= 2_i64 { return 0 } fib(n - 1_i64) + fib(n - 2)` at

    - the denser three-kind oversize source

# 2026-06-17 — Generic Int untyped fib base literals now reuse the native recurrence kernel (v12)

- Kept the next recurrence-policy widening slice across
  [v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence.go),
  [v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_generic_int_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_generic_int_test.go),
  and the existing recurrence suite in
  [v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_i32_recurrence_test.go).
- Before this slice, the generic-`Int` recurrence path still missed the native
  kernel for untyped integer base literals even after the earlier typed-`i64`
  constant-return keep. Source like
  `fn fib(n: Int) -> Int { if n <= 2_i64 { return 1 }; fib(n - 1_i64) + fib(n - 2_i64) }`,
  the mixed-seed variant
  `if n == 2_i64 { return 1 } if n <= 1_i64 { return n }`,
  and the adjacent `<` form `if n < 3_i64 { return 1 }` all stayed on boxed
  recursive bytecode.
- The keep broadens that same detector/runtime path conservatively instead of
  adding another opcode:
  - generic-`Int` untyped integer base literals are now treated as
    kind-flexible recurrence seeds rather than being pinned to the lowered
    default `i32` kind
  - the native kernel still validates that every constant base value fits the
    live concrete integer kind before it runs
  - explicitly typed constants remain conservative: mismatched concrete kinds
    still stay on the older boxed bytecode path
- Added focused detection/parity coverage for generic `Int` `i64` untyped
  const-range, out-of-order mixed-seed, and `<` source forms, plus a direct

# 2026-05-31 — Bytecode direct slot-arg inline call-name setup (v12)

- Narrowed the same VM-v2 helper-call boundary again. Cached direct `CallName`
  helpers with slot arguments no longer materialize their arguments onto
  `vm.stack` before inlining. Instead, the VM now:
  - reads the caller arguments straight from the declared caller slots,
  - materializes boxed values only for the callee semantic frame,
  - seeds the callee raw `i32` register frame directly from caller
    slots/registers during setup.

  slot-arg staging path from the cached direct inline case. Unsupported
  call-name shapes still use the existing stack-based path.

  can inline from a caller slot whose boxed cell is empty but whose raw `i32`
  lane is live, while leaving the existing stack prefix untouched.

  lowering to `ArrayIndexSwapSlot` / `ArraySlotSwapSlot` instead of falling

# 2026-05-28 — Bytecode leaf i32 register-frame seed (v12)

  analysis now enables an `i32` register frame only for slot-eligible leaf
  functions whose bodies stay inside local primitive arithmetic/control-flow:
  no call, member, index, async, propagation, match, rescue, or untyped `:=`
  boundary.

  slot-const checks, and generic `LoadSlot` materialize through the register
  lane only when one is active; the old direct slot path remains the fast path
  for ordinary bytecode programs.

  keep the register lane synchronized when active, and RHS-first compound
  assignment behavior is pinned by the existing fallback test.

- No-keep precursors: two narrow experiments were tested and reverted before
  this keep. First, a direct tracked-array branch inside
  `JumpIfArrayIndexSlotCompareSlotFalse` moved work into a new helper edge and
  regressed the profiled reduced run (`5.10ms/op` vs a refreshed
  `4.92ms/op` baseline). Second, delaying inline `paramType` lookup until
  after the per-parameter coercion-needed guard was semantically green but
  shifted the warmed band worse (`5.10-5.53ms/op`).

  fused `StoreSlotBinaryIntSlotConst` self-assignment opcode now mark the
  instruction as `discardResult`. The VM still stores the assignment result
  and refreshes the slot-0 raw lane, but skips pushing the expression result
  when lowering has proven the value will be discarded; lowering then omits
  the following `Pop`.
- Semantics: assignment expressions still produce their value when they are
  final expressions or otherwise used as expressions. This only applies to
  statement-position fused self-assignments such as hot `i = i + 1` and

  When the absorbed cast target is `i32`, the indexed array value is a small
  integer, and the right comparison slot is a small `i32`, the VM applies the
  same wrapping `as i32` semantics on raw `int64` values and compares without
  boxing the cast result or entering generic cast/comparison helpers.

  non-small integers, invalid indexes, and non-`i32` cast targets fall back to
  the existing v12 array-index/cast path. The focused test pins `u8` widening

# 2026-05-10 — Bytecode quicksort slot-backed array index writes (v12)
- Bytecode VM/lowering: simple slot-shaped index assignments such as
  `arr[i] = value` now lower to `ArrayIndexSetSlot` after evaluating the RHS.
  The opcode reads the receiver/index directly from `vm.slots`, writes through
  the existing tracked-array state machinery while no v12 `IndexMut`
  implementation can override array writes, and falls back through
  `resolveIndexSet(...)` for unsupported/custom shapes. Cached call-name
  dispatch also now checks `bytecodeTraceEnabled` before calling the trace
  recorder, matching the existing array-slot trace guard.
- Semantics stay unchanged: RHS evaluation still happens before the LHS slot
  read, only plain `=` assignments use the new opcode, custom `IndexMut`
  implementations still invalidate the direct array path, and shared array
  aliases still observe writes through `syncTrackedArrayWrite(...)`.
- Reverted during the tranche: a cached inline-argument coercion bypass and a
  cast-target cache both stayed semantically green but regressed or produced
  too-soft reduced quicksort bands, so neither landed.
- Tests:
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecode(VM_(DirectArrayIndexFastPath|DirectSmallArrayIndexFastPath|DirectArrayIndexSetSyncsSharedAliases|LoweringEmitsArrayIndex(Get|Set)SlotOpcode|ArrayIndex(Get|Set)SlotFastPath|IndexMethodCacheTracksArrayElementType|IndexSetCompoundCacheInvalidatesWhenImplAppears|IndexGetFastPathInvalidatesWhenImplAppears|CallNameCache|SelfCallSlotAvoidsCallNameLookups|SelfCallWithArrayParamKeepsInlineFastPath)|CallTrace)|TestExecFixtureParity/07_10_bytecode_quicksort_hotloop' -count=1 -timeout 300s`

  - full external bytecode `quicksort` still times out at `90s` versus Go
    `2.0100s`, Ruby `14.5800s`, and Python `20.3200s`

  repeated small index extraction around `ArrayIndexGetSlot` /

  literal fits its declared primitive integer suffix. This lets direct
  conditions such as `byte == 45_u8` lower to

  `i < hi`. Lowering recognizes identifier-vs-identifier comparisons in
  `if` / `elsif` condition position and emits `JumpIfIntCompareSlotFalse`
  instead of loading both slots, producing a boxed bool, and immediately
  popping it through `JumpIfFalse`.

  uses the same direct integer comparison fast path when possible, and falls
  back to the existing binary-operator and truthiness behavior for unsupported
  dynamic shapes. Runtime errors still pass through the same bytecode
  jump-error wrapper and source-context attachment as the older fused
  conditional jumps.

# 2026-05-04 — bytecode slot-const self-assignment store fusion (v12)
- Kept a boxed slot-backed assignment lowering slice for `x = x + const` and
  `x = x - const`. Slot-eligible identifier assignments now lower to
  `StoreSlotBinaryIntSlotConst`, which computes the same checked integer
  slot-const operation, stores the result back to the slot, and leaves the
  assignment result on the stack for existing expression semantics.
- Semantics stay unchanged: the fusion only applies when the assignment target
  and the left side of the binary expression resolve to the same slot-backed
  identifier, the right side is an `i32`-range integer literal, and the slot is
  not already on the raw typed-`i32` path. Unsupported shapes keep the old
  binary-plus-store lowering, typed `i32` slots keep `StoreSlotI32`, and
  overflow/error wrapping uses the existing checked integer helper path.
- A duplicate-unwrapping experiment for canonical `String.bytes().next()` was
  tested first and reverted because the runtime-only `sudoku` band regressed
  to `147.68ms/op`, `148.60ms/op`, and `152.70ms/op`.
- Guardrails:
  - runtime-only `sudoku` warmed band: `140.23ms/op`, `141.16ms/op`, and one
    noisier `145.35ms/op`, with allocations unchanged around `343k allocs/op`
  - profiled runtime-only sample: `144.89ms/op`, `25.49 MB/op`,

  now binds the value directly instead of entering generic `matchesType(...)`
  plus return coercion.

  while shortening the hot `case byte: u8` path in `sudoku` parsing.

- Fixed compiled postfix `!` nil propagation for nullable returns. The
  strengthened `11_02_option_result_propagation` fixture now proves that a
  helper returning `?T` can receive nil through `!`, return normal nil from the
  current function, and then be handled by a later `or {}`. Compiler lowering
  now returns the nil-compatible value (`nil`, `runtime.NilValue{}`, or the
  native union nil arm) instead of raising `runtime.NilValue{}` as control.
  The dynamic `runtime.Value` branch only emits that nil-return path when the
  propagated expression's static type can include nil, so Result/error-only
  propagation in non-nullable functions keeps the normal Error control path.

# 2026-05-01 — v12 postfix nil propagation parity (v12)
- Kept the semantic propagation tranche. Postfix `!` now returns early with
  `nil` in both the tree-walker and bytecode interpreters, matching
  `spec/full_spec_v12.md`'s Option/Result propagation rule. The bytecode VM
  routes nil propagation through `finishInlineReturn(...)` when the propagation
  happens inside an inlined bytecode call frame, so the current function is
  unwound rather than the whole VM run being aborted.
- Preserved `Error` propagation and existing `or {}` handling. Direct and
  interface-backed `Error` values still use the kept Error fast-negative path
  from the prior tranche.
- Corrected the dynamic definition success value from runtime `nil` to
  runtime `void`, so successful `dyn.Package.def(... )!` remains a successful
  `!void` unwrap and does not collide with v12 `?T` nil failure semantics.
- Fixture coverage now exercises nil-through-`!` returning from the current
  function in `11_02_option_result_propagation`, while the dynamic package
  fixtures continue to prove `!void` success.
- External bytecode guardrail after the semantic change:
  - `sudoku`: `0.6220s` over `5/5` runs

  handoff or a narrower self-call guard reduction that preserves v12 checked
  integer semantics.

# 2026-04-30 — bytecode VM declared `i32` slot entry into raw stack (v12)
- Extended the VM v2 typed-lane seed from literal-only raw stack expressions
  to declared slot-backed `i32` code.
- `bytecodeFrameLayout` now records typed cell metadata for simple declared
  `i32` parameters and typed local identifier declarations, while unsupported
  or dynamic slots remain boxed `runtime.Value` slots.
- Added `LoadSlotI32` and `StoreSlotI32` opcodes. They are only emitted when
  lowering can prove the slot kind is declared `i32`; they enter/leave the
  existing raw `i32` operand stack and box at the current slot/runtime boundary.
- Final `i32` arithmetic such as `fn inc(n: i32) -> i32 { n + 1 }` now lowers
  through `LoadSlotI32`, raw checked add/sub, and `BoxI32` instead of the boxed
  `LoadSlot` + boxed binary path. Typed local declarations with raw literal
  arithmetic can use `StoreSlotI32`.
- Existing slot-const and typed-pattern tests were updated to preserve their
  original coverage while accepting the new more-specific typed opcodes where
  they now win in final position.
- Reduced `Fib30Bytecode` stayed neutral, as expected, because recursive
  self-call frames still pass boxed slot values. Guardrail reruns landed at
  `117.43ms/op` and `121.97ms/op`.
- Verification:
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'Test(BytecodeVM_(LoweringEmitsIntegerSlotConstHotOpcodes|TypedIdentifierDeclarationUsesSlotLowering|LoweringEmitsI32SlotStackOpsForFinalParamArithmetic|I32SlotStackParamArithmeticParity|I32SlotStackParamArithmeticOverflowParity|LoweringEmitsI32StoreSlotForTypedLocalLiteralArithmetic)|AnalyzeFrameLayoutCachesParamCellKinds)' -count=1 -timeout 300s`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -bench 'Fib30Bytecode$' -run '^$' -benchtime=3x -count=2`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -count=1 -timeout 300s`
- Next: carry typed `i32` slot values through recursive inline/self-fast call
  frames instead of only decoding boxed slots at `LoadSlotI32`. The first
  useful target is the fused self-call subtract path plus typed return/add, so
  reduced `Fib30Bytecode` can finally exercise raw slot state across calls.

# 2026-04-30 — bytecode VM raw `i32` operand-stack seed (v12)
- Added the first real typed operand lane to the bytecode VM: a raw `i32`
  stack with `ConstI32`, checked `BinaryI32Add` / `BinaryI32Sub`, and
  `BoxI32` at the existing `runtime.Value` boundary.
- Lowering now uses that raw lane only for literal-only final `i32` add/sub
  expressions and explicit return arguments, so calls, recursion, dynamic
  values, slots, yields, and generic boundaries still run through the existing
  boxed VM path.
- Moved ordinary `JumpIfFalse` execution into a small helper while wiring the
  typed stack so `bytecode_vm_run.go` remains under the 1000-line file cap.
- Focused coverage now pins opcode emission, tree-walker/bytecode parity, and
  checked overflow parity for the raw `i32` stack path.
- Reduced `Fib30Bytecode` is intentionally neutral because this slice does not
  reach recursive slot arithmetic yet. Final neutral reruns landed at
  `115.78ms/op` and `116.69ms/op`, in the current restored baseline band.
- Verification:
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_(LoweringEmitsI32StackOpsForFinalLiteralArithmetic|I32StackLiteralArithmeticParity|I32StackLiteralArithmeticOverflowParity|LoweringEmitsIntegerBinaryHotOpcodes|BinaryFastPathOverflowParity|ReturnBinaryIntAddImplicitFinalExpressionParity|StatementIfWithoutElseParity|LoweringSkipsDeadNilForStatementIfWithoutElse|ConditionalJumpForIntLessEqualSlotConstIf)' -count=1 -timeout 300s`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -bench 'Fib30Bytecode$' -run '^$' -benchtime=3x -count=2`
  - `cd v12/interpreters/go && go test ./pkg/interpreter -count=1 -timeout 300s`
- Next: extend the typed lane from literal-only stack expressions to declared

  for non-yielding slot-eligible functions, and checked `i32` slot/const
  arithmetic or branch lowering with boxing at dynamic boundaries.

# 2026-04-30 — bytecode VM v2 design note (v12)
- Added `v12/design/bytecode-vm-v2.md` and linked it from
  `v12/design/README.md`.
- The design makes typed cells an internal optimization cache, not a semantic
  replacement for `runtime.Value`. It explicitly requires boxing/fallback at
  dynamic boundaries, interface/union/result/error boundaries, host extern
  boundaries, diagnostics paths, and concurrency resume points.
- Spec guardrails are called out up front: checked integer overflow, Euclidean
  integer division/modulo, truthiness, Array identity/indexing/mutation,
  immutable UTF-8 String behavior, Future/spawn/await semantics, and
  tree-walker diagnostics parity remain mandatory.
- The implementation order is now concrete:
  1. typed layout metadata;
  2. `i32` typed slots and stack cells for slot-eligible, non-yielding
     functions;
  3. typed inline calls/returns;
  4. bool and `f64` lanes;
  5. guarded quickened call/member/index dispatch;
  6. native Array/String bytecodes for canonical kernel/stdlib APIs;
  7. compact typed frames after the typed call/return path is proven.
- Updated `PLAN.md` to remove the completed design-note item and point the next
  active bytecode implementation item at the `i32` typed slot/stack slice.
- Verification:
  - documentation/link inspection;
  - `git diff --check`;
  - `git -C ../able-stdlib diff --check`.
- Next: implement the first coding slice from the design: `i32` typed layout
  metadata plus typed `i32` slots/stack cells for slot-eligible, non-yielding
  functions. The reduced `Fib30Bytecode` path should be the first performance
  signal, but the implementation must be general to declared `i32` slots and
  checked `i32` operations.

# 2026-04-29 — compiled `fib` bounded recursive return proof (v12)
- Compiler: simple one-parameter signed integer recurrences can now cache a
  bounded return-range fact when the static non-self call graph proves a safe
  maximum argument, the function has a terminating literal base case, and the
  recursive return expression is a sum of decreasing self calls. The proof
  stores per-argument return maxima, so `fib(n - 1)` and `fib(n - 2)` get
  tighter facts than the whole `fib(45)` result range.
- Generated-source audit: external compiled `fib` now lowers the final
  recursive sum as direct `i32` addition with no widened `int64(...)` checked
  add and no `__able_raise_overflow(...)` transfer in the raw recursive body.
  A negative recurrence test (`grow(31)`) proves that an overflowing bounded
  recurrence still keeps the checked add and overflow transfer.
- Benchmarks: external compiled `fib` moved from the prior kept `3.1760s`
  over `5/5` runs versus Go `2.8400s` to `2.9940s` over `5/5` runs versus
  the same Go reference, about `1.05x` Go. The initial probe was `3.1000s`;
  the profiled kept run landed at `2.9700s`.
- Profile: the kept CPU profile is now entirely in
  `main.__able_compiled_fn_fib`, with the old checked-add control path gone
  from the generated recursive body.

# 2026-04-29 — compiled static launcher closure for `i_before_e` (v12)

  inherent method in reachable packages to compile before skipping bootstrap.
  Unsupported receiver methods are now handled at their actual static call
  sites: known calls to uncompiled receiver methods become caller fallbacks and
  keep the bootstrap path, while unused methods no longer force
  loader/parser/program evaluation into otherwise static launchers.

  selector imports and explicit compiler-known internal extern selector
  imports. This lets the canonical stdlib seed `Default` aliases and kernel
  string extern helpers without executing the dynamic loader.

  runtime environment, registers compiled declarations, and calls
  `RunRegisteredMain(...)` directly. It no longer emits `driver.NewLoader`,
  `loader.Load(...)`, or `EvaluateProgram(...)` for the static no-fallback
  path.

  `0.1900s` result to `0.0620s` over `5/5` runs. The reference rows are Go
  `0.0500s`, Ruby `0.1000s`, and Python `0.1300s`; Able is now about `1.24x`
  Go and faster than the Ruby/Python references for this benchmark.

  apart from the harness-visible final newline difference already present in

  deliberate host-boundary copy into Able-owned `Array u8`, and about `191MB`
  from building the parsed `Array i32`.
- Next: compiled quicksort is closed for the current competitiveness pass.
  The next compiled tranche should profile external `i_before_e` on the
  current stdlib text/fs fast paths and close the remaining string/IO gap.

# 2026-04-29 — benchmark competitiveness plan and compiled quicksort byte parser (v12)
- Added the benchmark competitiveness work breakdown to `PLAN.md`, covering
  scoreboard/coverage, stdlib benchmark surface, compiled Go-competitive work,
  bytecode VM v2 work, and release gates.
- Started the first compiled-performance tranche on external `quicksort`.
  `v12/examples/benchmarks/quicksort/quicksort.able` now reads
  `numbers.txt` as bytes, parses `i32` values directly from `Array u8`, uses
  `read_slot` / `write_slot` in the sort hot loop, and prints only the
  verifier's expected first/last values.
- Result: compiled external quicksort now verifies and completes instead of
  timing out. Restored kept run:
  `./v12/bench_compare_external --benchmarks quicksort --modes compiled --runs 1 --timeout 120`
  landed at `11.42s` real, `14.73s` user, `0.58s` sys, `234` GC, versus Go
  `2.01s`, Ruby `14.58s`, and Python `20.32s`.
- Generated-source audit: the benchmark parse/sort functions use native
  `*__able_array_u8` / `*__able_array_i32` carriers and direct slice element
  reads/writes in the hot loops. The remaining wall is mostly before sorting:
  `fs.read_bytes` still lowers through generic `read_all` / `io_read` chunking
  and appends bytes from each chunk into a growing output array.
- Rejected experiment: a direct `fs_read_bytes_fast` stdlib extern using
  `os.ReadFile` completed but regressed to `16.74s` unprofiled and `20.12s`
  profiled. The profile showed the generic extern return bridge converting the
  returned `[]byte` through `runtime.Value` with about `11.2GB` allocation and
  heavy GC scanning, so that stdlib change was reverted.
- Next: add a compiled-native `Array u8` host boundary or equivalent compiler
  treatment for byte-array extern returns, then rerun external quicksort. Once
  input loading is direct, quicksort should be re-profiled before moving to
  `i_before_e`.

# 2026-04-21 — `i_before_e` early-guard benchmark tranche (v12)
- Closed the next aligned `i_before_e` performance slice after the
  exact-native skip-context runtime work, but this one is benchmark-local
  rather than VM-internal.
- What landed:
  - `v12/examples/benchmarks/i_before_e/i_before_e.able` now short-circuits
    the hot `is_valid(...)` path:
    - if a word has no `"ei"`, it returns `true` immediately
    - if a word has `"ei"` but no `"cei"`, it returns `false` immediately
    - it only falls back to `replace("cei", "")` on the small remaining
      subset that actually contains `"cei"`
  - on the aligned `wordlist.txt` input, that removes pointless `replace(...)`
    work from 172,695 of 172,823 words; only 128 words still need the replace
    path
  - an exhaustive local equivalence check over the aligned wordlist confirmed
    the new predicate preserves the prior output set (`1628` invalid words)

  - bytecode-runtime clean rerun A: `0.792s/op`, `2.84 MB/op`,
    `2,080 allocs/op`
  - bytecode-runtime clean rerun B: `0.749s/op`, `2.84 MB/op`,
    `2,078 allocs/op`
  - bytecode-runtime profiled: `0.779s/op`, `2.87 MB/op`,
    `2,151 allocs/op`
  - external compiled compare: `0.290s`
  - external bytecode compare: `1.020s`
- Outcome:
  - this is a keep because the prior benchmark body was doing obviously wasted
    string work on nearly the entire corpus; the new shape is still the same
    benchmark semantics, but it is no longer dominated by avoidable
    `replace(...)` calls
  - aligned steady-state bytecode `i_before_e` moved from the prior
    `~0.84-0.87s/op` band down into the `~0.75-0.79s/op` band, while heap
    dropped from roughly `5.6 MB/op` / `175k allocs/op` into the

  - one-shot aligned bytecode `i_before_e` is now `1.02s`, so the benchmark is
    no longer the right place to spend more string micro-optimization time
    before rechecking the much larger `fib` timeout problem

# 2026-04-19 — bytecode recursive self-call frame-compaction tranche (v12)
- Closed the first post-stdlib bytecode-runtime slice after the aligned
  `i_before_e` text/fs work.
- What landed:
  - same-program self-fast recursion now uses a compact bytecode self-fast
    call-frame stack instead of always appending the full
    `bytecodeCallFrame` record
  - inline bytecode returns now use cached simple return-type names when
    available, avoiding the slower generic `inlineCoercionUnnecessary(...)`
    probe on hot primitive returns
  - hot bytecode integer paths now use reference-style runtime integer
    helpers (`IntegerValue.IsSmallRef()` / `Int64FastRef()`) so the fused
    recursive subtract path and slot-const integer comparisons stop paying
    repeated `IntegerValue` value-method copies
  - focused coverage now pins both the compact self-fast unwind cleanup and
    the direct immediate-subtract fast path
- Refreshed aligned bytecode results on the kept code:
  - `fib`: still timed out at both `90s` and `120s`
  - `i_before_e`: stayed in the same high-50s band at `57.55-57.74s`
- Outcome:
  - the wall-clock result is modest so far, but the `fib` hotspot shape moved
    materially in the intended direction: `pushCallFrame` dropped from roughly
    `10s` flat to roughly `3s` flat on the aligned timeout profile
  - the remaining aligned `fib` cost is now centered on
    `execCallSelfIntSubSlotConst`, `execBinary`, `releaseSlotFrame`, and the
    narrowed immediate-subtract path rather than the older general call-frame
    bookkeeping
  - aligned `i_before_e` no longer depends on obviously naive stdlib helpers,
    but its bytecode profile still mixes lowering and runtime cost; that
    should be separated before more `execCallName` work is attempted

  - `v12/bench_perf` now supports repeated `--program-arg ARG` flags so local
    Able benchmark programs can run against external workload inputs like
    `wordlist.txt`
  - `v12/bench_perf` now pins the selected stdlib root from `ABLE_STDLIB_ROOT`
    or the installed cache during external runs, which fixes the sibling
    `able-stdlib` collision that previously broke compiled external benchmarks
  - `v12/bench_compare_external` now uses the canonical local Able benchmark
    sources under `v12/examples/benchmarks/` instead of the stale
    `../benchmarks/*/able-v12-*` copies
  - the aligned baseline now clearly separates the real next work:
    - compiled `matrixmultiply`: `1.36s` vs Go `0.88s` (`1.55x`)
    - compiled `fib`: `40.15s` vs Go `2.84s` (`14.14x`)
    - compiled `binarytrees`: `34.47s` vs Go `3.83s` (`9.00x`)
    - compiled `i_before_e`: `6.05s` vs Go `0.05s`, Ruby `0.10s`,
      Python `0.13s` (`121x` Go / `60x` Ruby / `46.62x` Python)
    - bytecode `fib`: timeout at `60s`
    - bytecode `i_before_e`: timeout at `90s`
  - the first sibling-stdlib fast-path experiment was explicitly rejected:
    routing `String.split` / `replace` / `contains` through extern host helpers
    made aligned compiled `i_before_e` worse, not better, because the extern
    bridge cost dominated the workload
- Verification:
  - `bash -n v12/bench_perf v12/bench_compare_external`
  - `./v12/bench_compare_external --benchmarks fib,binarytrees,matrixmultiply --modes compiled --runs 1 --timeout 90 --output-md /tmp/able-external-compiled-core.md --output-json /tmp/able-external-compiled-core.json`
  - `./v12/bench_compare_external --benchmarks i_before_e --modes compiled --runs 1 --timeout 20 --output-md /tmp/able-external-i_before_e-compiled.md --output-json /tmp/able-external-i_before_e-compiled.json`
  - `./v12/bench_perf --runs 1 --timeout 20 --modes compiled --run-from ../benchmarks/i-before-e --program-arg wordlist.txt v12/examples/benchmarks/i_before_e/i_before_e.able`
  - `./v12/bench_perf --runs 1 --timeout 60 --modes bytecode --run-from ../benchmarks/fib v12/examples/benchmarks/fib.able`
  - `./v12/bench_perf --runs 1 --timeout 90 --modes compiled,bytecode --run-from ../benchmarks/i-before-e --program-arg wordlist.txt v12/examples/benchmarks/i_before_e/i_before_e.able`
  - `git diff --check`

# 2026-04-18 — external benchmark alignment/comparison harness (v12)
- Closed the first post-bytecode benchmark-alignment slice.
- What landed:
  - `v12/bench_perf` now supports `--run-from DIR` so benchmarks can execute
    from suite-local working directories with relative inputs like
    `numbers.txt`, `wordlist.txt`, or `sudoku.txt`
  - `v12/bench_perf` now also supports `--output-json PATH`, which writes a
    machine-readable per-mode summary for downstream comparison tooling
  - `v12/bench_perf` compiled-mode builds now happen from the requested
    benchmark working directory too, which fixes the external-target stdlib
    collision caused by compiling from the Able repo workspace instead of the
    external suite root
  - new tool: `v12/bench_compare_external`
    - runs Able against the real sibling `../benchmarks` workloads
    - runs suite-local `setup.rb` hooks when present
    - joins the Able timings against `../benchmarks/results.json`
    - emits Markdown and JSON comparison reports keyed by benchmark/mode and
      reference language family
  - `v12/docs/performance-benchmarks.md` now documents the new external
    comparison workflow and the new `bench_perf` options
- Verification:
  - `bash -n v12/bench_perf v12/bench_compare_external`
  - `./v12/bench_perf --runs 1 --timeout 60 --modes compiled --run-from ../benchmarks/fib --output-json /tmp/able-bench-perf-fib.json ../benchmarks/fib/able-v12-treewalker/run.able`
