## 2026-06-26 — keep per-block bytecode runtime scope emission (v12)

- Scope:
  - shared bytecode block-scope lowering/runtime policy only
  - no benchmark-shaped opcode, lowering rule, or specialized code generation
- What changed:
  - `bytecodeLoweringContext` now tracks lexical scopes as either runtime
    environment scopes, slot-only scopes, or both, instead of assuming every
    lexical block implies a runtime environment shell
  - `emitBlock(...)` now emits runtime `EnterScope` / `ExitScope` only when
    the current block itself directly introduces env-registered definitions
    (`struct`, `union`, `type`, `interface`, `extern`, `import`,
    `dynimport`) or, in env-backed programs, direct local declarations that
    truly need a fresh lexical environment
  - slot-frame blocks still get slot-scope isolation when they introduce slot
    locals, but those slot-only scopes no longer force a runtime environment
    allocation
  - slot-lowered `match` clauses now create a scope only when the clause
    actually binds a slot-backed identifier, instead of always wrapping the
    clause body in a lexical shell
  - loop `break` / `continue` lowering now counts only runtime scopes to
    unwind, so loop bodies with zero runtime scopes do not emit redundant
    `ExitScope` bytecode
  - the VM runtime `bytecodeOpEnterScope` / `bytecodeOpExitScope` path now
    obeys the lowered runtime-scope count via `instr.argCount`
- Added guardrails:
  - `bytecode_scope_lowering_test.go` now checks:
    - pure env-backed `if` blocks lower without runtime scope bytecode
    - env-backed blocks with a direct declaration still emit one runtime scope
    - slot-frame functions with a nested env-defining branch emit a runtime
      scope only for that direct branch block
    - bytecode loop `continue` still works when the loop body has zero runtime
      scopes to unwind
- Verification:
  - focused lowering/loop/scope slice:
    - `env GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeLoweringSkipsEnvScopeForPureIfBlocks|TestBytecodeLoweringEmitsEnvScopeForIfBlockDeclaration|TestBytecodeLoweringEmitsRuntimeScopeOnlyForDirectEnvBlockInSlotFunction|TestBytecodeVMLoopContinueWithoutRuntimeScopes|TestBytecodeVM_MatchGuardBindingDoesNotLeakToOuterScope|TestBytecodeVM_RescueGuardBindingDoesNotLeakToOuterScope|TestLoopExpressionMatchesExampleLoop' -count=1`
    - result: `ok able/interpreter-go/pkg/interpreter 0.078s`
- Runtime signal:
  - pre-change bounded samples from the immediately preceding profile tranche:
    - `word_count_small`: `1729348717 ns/op`, `297307152 B/op`,
      `6044273 allocs/op`
    - `binarytrees_small`: `460768852 ns/op`, `97892784 B/op`,
      `686282 allocs/op`
  - clean sequential reruns after the keep:
    - `word_count_small`: `1579945637 ns/op`, `245949312 B/op`,
      `5508729 allocs/op`
    - bounded profile rerun: `1594079892 ns/op`, `245927544 B/op`,
      `5508667 allocs/op`
    - `binarytrees_small`: `470066523 ns/op`, `97234232 B/op`,
      `675343 allocs/op`
- Profile implication:
  - refreshed bounded `word_count_small` alloc profile:
    - `runtime.newEnvironmentBase(...)` drops from about `944892` sampled
      alloc objects to about `447867`
    - direct `runResumable(...) -> NewEnvironment(...)` drops from about
      `688188` sampled alloc objects to about `180239`
    - remaining `NewEnvironmentWithValueCapacity(...)` callers are now led by
      `matchPatternFast(...)` at about `234857`, then the residual
      `runResumable(...) -> NewEnvironment(...)` path at about `180239`, with
      explicit call-environment seeding down at about `32771`
    - overall top allocators now skew more toward
      `bytecodeStackSnapshotValue(...)`, raw integer slot churn
      (`storeRawIntegerSlot(...)` / `math/big.nat.make`), and string-builder

- Outcome:
  - this keep is generic and semantically grounded: it reduces shared runtime
    environment churn by tightening block-scope emission policy, not by
    specializing any benchmark shape
  - the refreshed profile confirms the intended wall moved materially, so this
    change clears the bar to keep
- Next target:

    (`matchPatternFast(...)` plus the residual `runResumable(...)`

## 2026-06-26 — keep bindingless match/rescue clause env reuse with direct-binding guardrails (v12)

- Scope:

  - no benchmark-shaped opcode, lowering rule, or specialized code generation
- What changed:
  - added conservative `expressionNeedsCurrentScopeBinding(...)` and
    `clauseNeedsLocalScope(...)` helpers so the interpreter can distinguish:
    - clauses that truly need a fresh lexical env because the pattern binds or
      the guard/body can directly define into the current scope
    - bindingless clauses whose guard/body are pure with respect to the
      current scope and can therefore reuse the outer env safely
  - `matchPatternForClause(...)` now routes through a scope-reuse-aware fast
    path and returns the outer env directly when the clause is bindingless and
    does not need its own declaration scope
  - tree-walker `match` / `rescue` and bytecode `runMatchExpression(...)` /
    `execRescue(...)` now use that clause-aware entry point
- Added guardrails:
  - `scope_capacity_test.go` now checks that:
    - nested block declarations do not force clause-local scope
    - pattern bindings, guard-local declarations, and direct clause-body
      declarations still do
  - `interpreter_patterns_test.go` now checks that:
    - a bindingless pure literal clause reuses the base env
    - a direct clause declaration still forces a fresh env
  - existing semantic tests stay in the focused slice:
    - direct declaration in a literal clause remains scoped
    - guard-created bindings remain visible to the clause body
    - match/rescue guard bindings still do not leak in either runtime

## 2026-06-27 — keep tracked i32 array-cache growth generic (v12)

- Scope:
  - shared tracked-array metadata/caching on the bytecode path
  - no benchmark-shaped opcode, lowering rule, or specialized code generation
- What changed:
  - `refreshTrackedArrayI32RawCache(...)` now reuses existing cache backing
    when the current slices already have enough capacity instead of allocating
    fresh `[]int32` / `[]bool` storage on every rebuild
  - typed `runtime.NilValue{}` slots now behave like array holes for tracked
    `i32` cache purposes, so writes of `nil` into non-zero positions invalidate
    only that slot instead of throwing away the whole partial cache
  - tracked cache growth is now handled with a local geometric capacity policy
    that matches the runtime's normal array growth shape rather than exact-
    length reallocation on every append-sized expansion
  - conservative growth reuse only applies when the already-cached prefix is
    still valid and every newly visible slot except the current write remains a
    hole; otherwise the code still falls back to full cache refresh
- Important adjustment during the tranche:
  - the first draft reused the new resize helper but grew cache slices at exact
    length; that regressed the bounded heap benchmark badly (`~237MB/op`) by
    forcing repeated full-slice reallocations on append-heavy paths
  - that exact-length growth policy was removed before keeping anything and
    replaced with geometric growth; the final kept state does not include the
    regressing version
- Why this keep stayed generic:
  - the new logic only changes shared tracked-array cache maintenance rules
    around holes, cache reuse, and slice growth
  - no code generation path, benchmark source, or named stdlib/container type
    received special handling
- Added guardrails:
  - `interpreter_array_tracking_test.go` now checks that:
    - full cache refresh treats typed `nil` slots as holes
    - writing typed `nil` into an `i32` tracked array invalidates only the
      written cache slot
    - cached `i32` metadata extends correctly across typed-`nil` growth
    - repeated cache refresh reuses existing backing without allocating
  - `bytecode_vm_array_index_swap_test.go` now accepts either uncached or
    already-cached raw-first tracked states while still asserting the post-swap
    cached `i32` values
- Verification:
  - focused tracked-array/cache slice:
    - `go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'Test(RefreshTrackedArrayI32RawCacheTreatsNilValuesAsHoles|RefreshTrackedArrayI32RawCacheReusesBacking|InterpreterSyncTrackedArrayWrite(BuildsPartialCachedI32ValuesForHoleyArray|NilInvalidatesOnlyTargetCachedI32Slot|AppendExtendsCachedI32Values|ExtendsCachedI32ValuesAcrossTypedNilGrowth)|InterpreterSyncArrayHandleLength(KeepsCachedI32ValuesOnTrim|FromEmptyUsesNilToken)|BytecodeVM_Array(IndexSwapSlotI32FastPathHandlesRawTrackedI32|SlotSwapSlotTrackedFastPathUpdatesCachedI32Values))' -count=1`

    - `go test ./pkg/runtime -run 'Test(AdjustArrayI32CacheLength(ShrinkPreservesKnownEntries|GrowAppendsInvalidSlots)|ArrayStateBoxed(Length|Capacity)UsesSharedMetadataCache|BoxedArrayMetadataU64ValueUsesSharedCache)' -count=1`

## 2026-06-29 — Back out generic named-struct positional widening; keep shared named-field index cache (v12)

## 2026-06-29 — Remove residual stable call-shell copies and build match clause envs lazily (v12)

- Scope:
  - shared bytecode generic `call`, `call_name`, and `call_member` arg
    preparation when callee stability requires copying
  - shared `matchPatternForClause(...)` scope construction for
    struct/array/literal/typed match patterns
  - no benchmark-shaped opcode, lowering rule, or nominal/container-specific
    specialization
- What changed:
  - added
    [bytecodePrepareCallArgsIntoBuffer(...)](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_call_args.go:111)
    in
    [bytecode_call_args.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_call_args.go:1)
    so small stable arg shells can be materialized into caller-owned inline
    storage instead of always cloning into heap slices
  - updated
    [bytecode_vm_calls.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_calls.go:758),
    [bytecode_vm_call_name_cache.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_call_name_cache.go:301),
    and
    [bytecode_vm_call_member.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_call_member.go:820)
    so the shared generic bytecode call shells use that inline buffer path
    before falling back to `bytecodePrepareCallArgs(..., true)`
  - added regression coverage in
    [call_args_mutation_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/call_args_mutation_test.go:226)
    to confirm the new inline path preserves stable-copy semantics and does
    not mutate the caller arg slice
  - changed
    [interpreter_patterns.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter_patterns.go:195)
    so `matchPatternForClause(...)` uses
    `matchPatternIntoClauseEnv(...)` plus
    `matchPatternClauseBindingEnv(...)` to build the clause environment
    lazily during recursive pattern matching instead of first collecting a
    transient binding slice and then calling `NewEnvironmentWithBindings(...)`
  - kept the existing `matchPatternFastWithScopeReuse(...)` short-circuit and
    the existing struct/array/literal/typed pattern semantics; the change is
    only in how the shared scope is seeded once a clause needs bindings
  - tried a smaller stack-backed binding-slice helper first, profiled it, and
    removed it before finishing because the slice storage escaped and did not
    produce a real shared win
- Why this keep stayed generic:
  - the inline arg-copy path applies to arbitrary bytecode calls whose callee
    requires stable args; it is shared call plumbing, not a fixture shape
  - the lazy clause-env construction applies to arbitrary match patterns and
    preserves the same binding order, shadowing, typed coercion, and
    bindingless-match reuse semantics as the prior slice-seeding path
  - no new opcode, fused benchmark stencil, or library-type-specific
    dispatch/lowering rule was added
- Verification:
  - focused call/pattern/control slice:
    - `env GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'Test(BytecodePrepareCallArgsWithOptionalReceiver_DoesNotMutateSourceArgsOnStableCopy|BytecodePrepareCallArgsWithOptionalReceiverIntoBuffer_DoesNotMutateSourceArgs|BytecodePrepareCallArgsIntoBuffer_DoesNotMutateSourceArgsOnStableCopy|BytecodePrepareCallArgsIntoBuffer_RequiresStableCopy|BytecodeTraceStaticMemberCallsUseResolvedMethodPath|BytecodeVM_NativeBoundMethodExactCallInjectsReceiverOnce|BytecodeVM_NativeBoundMethodExactCallMaterializesComputedIntegerArg|BytecodeVM_NativeCallNameExactCallMaterializesComputedIntegerArg|BytecodeVM_NativeBoundMethodArgsStayStableWhenBorrowDisabled|BytecodeVM_NativeExactCallsSkipInlineProbeStats|BytecodeVM_NativeExactCallSkipContextPassesNilContext|BytecodeVM_CallMemberOpcodeExecutesMethodCall|BytecodeVM_CallMemberFallsBackToCallableField|BytecodeVM_CallMemberHandlesOptionalMethodArity|BytecodeResolveExactInjectedNativeCallTargetAcceptsNativeBoundMethod|BytecodeVM_CallNameScopeCacheInvalidatesOnLocalRebind|BytecodeVM_CallNameScopeCacheInvalidatesOnCapturedParentRebind|BytecodeVM_CallNameDotFallbackScopeCacheInvalidatesOnHeadRebind|AssignmentPattern|CompoundAssignmentPattern|BlockScope|ForLoopArraySum|MatchLiteralPatterns|MatchGuard|RescueExpression|OrElseExpression|BytecodeLinkedListIteratorFilterMapBenchWarmup)$' -count=1 -timeout 60s`
    - result: `ok able/interpreter-go/pkg/interpreter 0.704s`
  - bounded low-memory bytecode runtime spot-checks:
    - `linked_list_iterator_filter_map_i64_small`:
      - `476891177 ns/op`, `55677288 B/op`, `583676 allocs/op`
    - `word_count_small`:
      - `1479046472 ns/op`, `117988792 B/op`, `1278834 allocs/op`
  - refreshed linked-list alloc profile:

    - the next exposed generic leaders are now fresh env allocation

- Outcome:

    [bytecode_call_args.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_call_args.go)
    so resolved bytecode function-call prep now preserves raw numeric carriers
    for interpreted function calls instead of eagerly materializing them into
    boxed runtime scalars; stable-copy paths still copy when the call contract
    requires it, but they now copy the raw values directly
  - updated
    [bytecode_vm_call_member.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_call_member.go)
    so the direct resolved member-stack call path no longer rematerializes raw
    numeric args before handing them to the shared interpreter function-call
    path
  - updated
    [interpreter_type_info.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter_type_info.go),
    [call_helpers.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/call_helpers.go),
    and
    [eval_expressions_calls_overloads.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/eval_expressions_calls_overloads.go)
    so raw integer and raw float carriers participate directly in shared type
    inspection, generic type-argument inference, overload keying, and runtime
    mismatch reporting without forcing earlier boxing
  - updated
    [eval_expressions_calls.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/eval_expressions_calls.go)
    so compiled-thunk invocation materializes raw args at the thunk boundary
    itself, preserving the compiled/runtime contract while letting
    interpreter-only calls stay raw longer
  - extended
    [bytecode_call_args_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_call_args_test.go),
    [bytecode_vm_call_member_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_call_member_test.go),
    [bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value_test.go),
    and
    [eval_expressions_calls_state_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/eval_expressions_calls_state_test.go)
    with focused coverage for:
    - resolved-call arg prep keeping reusable raw `i32` stack cells raw
    - direct resolved member-stack invocation with a raw `i32` argument
    - raw numeric carrier type-expression inference
    - compiled thunks still receiving boxed `runtime.IntegerValue` args
- Why this keep stayed generic:
  - it changes the shared interpreter-side function call boundary rather than
    adding a benchmark-specific opcode, fused bytecode shape, or per-container
    lowering rule
  - raw carriers are now recognized by the same general type-info and overload
    metadata helpers used across the interpreter, which is broader than any
    single benchmark
  - compiled/native boundaries still decide when boxing is required, so the
    keep narrows eager materialization instead of weakening runtime contracts
- Verification:
  - focused resolved-call/raw-carrier regression slice:
    - `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'Test(BytecodeVM_(PrepareResolvedFunctionCallArgsWithOptionalReceiverInlineScratchHotAllocFree|PrepareResolvedFunctionCallArgsWithOptionalReceiverSpillScratchHotAllocFree|PrepareResolvedFunctionCallArgsPreservesRawI32StackCell|BinaryIntSubUsesReusableRawI32StackCellBeyondStaticCache|ReusableRawI32StackCellMaterializesForDivMod)|InterpreterTypeExpressionFromValueRecognizesRawNumericCarriers|CallCallableValue_(DirectCompiledThunkKeepsPayloadStateLazy|CompiledThunkMaterializesRawIntegerArgs)|Bytecode(LinkedListIteratorFilterMapBenchWarmup|HeapI32BenchWarmup))$' -count=1 -timeout 60s`
    - result: `ok able/interpreter-go/pkg/interpreter 5.387s`
  - additional focused follow-up:
    - `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_(TryCallResolvedCallableFromMemberStackPreservesRawI32Arg|PrepareResolvedFunctionCallArgsPreservesRawI32StackCell)|TestCallCallableValue_CompiledThunkMaterializesRawIntegerArgs|TestInterpreterTypeExpressionFromValueRecognizesRawNumericCarriers' -count=1`
    - result: `ok able/interpreter-go/pkg/interpreter 0.132s`
  - bounded low-memory bytecode-runtime spot-checks:
    - `heap_i32_small`:
      - before: `4802121564-4873951367 ns/op`,
        `5486608 B/op`, `48035 allocs/op`
      - after reruns: `4587332324-4784367083 ns/op`,
        `5486608 B/op`, `48035 allocs/op`
    - `persistent_sorted_set_i32_small`:
      - before: `2595895406 ns/op`, `340412384 B/op`, `2933939 allocs/op`
      - after: `2568568112 ns/op`, `340399696 B/op`, `2933927 allocs/op`
    - `word_count_small` control:
      - before: `1445658733 ns/op`, `96983680 B/op`, `1058319 allocs/op`
      - after reruns: `1484257030-1497555890 ns/op`,
        `96983632-96983808 B/op`, `1058316-1058325 allocs/op`
  - refreshed bounded `heap_i32_small` alloc profile:
    - sampled `bytecodePrepareCallArgs(...)` cumulative alloc objects drop
      from about `21846` to about `10923`
    - sampled `bytecodeMaterializeRawIntegerValue(...)` drops from about
      `76461` to about `43692`
    - the next shared wall moves to generic arithmetic/immediate-result paths
      (`execBinary`, `execBinarySlotConst`,
      `bytecodeMultiplyIntegerImmediateFast`,
      `bytecodeBoxedIntegerI32Value(...)`) rather than resolved-call arg prep
- Outcome:
  - kept
  - this trims a real shared call-boundary allocation source without changing
    native or compiled contracts, and it leaves the broader benchmark slice
    essentially stable while making the heap alloc profile materially cleaner
  - the result is that resolved interpreter-function calls are no longer the
    main reason raw `i32` values get boxed; the next remaining cost is in
    arithmetic/immediate result handling itself
- Next target:
  - move off resolved-call arg prep and target the remaining generic
    arithmetic/immediate-result boxing paths
  - this will entail profiling and tightening shared `i32` binary /
    slot-const / immediate arithmetic paths so they keep raw results longer
    and avoid unnecessary `bytecodeBoxedIntegerI32Value(...)` churn, because
    that is where the current heap alloc profile is now concentrated

## 2026-06-30 — Keep mono unsigned array writes handle-backed and trim typed-array deopts (v12)

- What changed:
  - updated
    [bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value.go)
    so shared raw integer results use lighter direct carriers for
    `u8` / `u16` / `u32` / `u64` / `usize`, and so the shared raw-value
    materializer / type-info helpers recognize those carriers directly
  - updated
    [bytecode_vm_float_slot_update.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_float_slot_update.go)
    so stack snapshots preserve the lighter raw integer carrier form instead
    of rebuilding the older generic raw-integer wrapper for unsigned results
  - updated
    [interpreter_type_matching.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter_type_matching.go)
    so shared `matchesType(Array<T>, ...)` first consults mono-array handle
    metadata and array size before falling back to boxed element
    materialization
  - updated
    [bytecode_vm_unsigned_array_fast.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_unsigned_array_fast.go)
    so mono `u32` array reads return the shared raw unsigned carrier instead
    of eagerly boxing through `runtime.IntegerValue`
  - updated
    [interpreter_arrays.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter_arrays.go),
    [bytecode_vm_array_slot_member_fast.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_array_slot_member_fast.go),
    [bytecode_vm_index_cache.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_index_cache.go),
    and
    [bytecode_vm_array_member_fast_array.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_array_member_fast_array.go)
    so handle-backed writes that preserve a mono typed-array handle now
    invalidate tracked value views instead of forcing
    `ArrayStoreState(handle)` to deopt the typed array into boxed dynamic
    state just to synchronize aliases
  - extended
    [bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value_test.go),
    [bytecode_vm_stack_snapshot_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_stack_snapshot_test.go),
    and
    [bytecode_vm_array_member_fast_unsigned_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_array_member_fast_unsigned_test.go)
    with focused coverage for:
    - direct unsigned raw-result carriers
    - mono-array type matching without materialization
    - mono `u32` read/write/index-set fast paths preserving the typed handle
      and avoiding boxed state materialization
- Why this keep stayed generic:
  - it removes overhead at shared VM/runtime boundaries that every typed-array
    workload can hit; it does not inspect a benchmark AST, container name, or
    fixed expression stencil
  - no benchmark-specific opcode, fused lowering rule, or named-container
    compiler special case was added; the change only adjusts general raw-value
    carriers, general type inspection, and general handle/view synchronization
  - the new handle-write invalidation keeps typed arrays typed until some
    later path actually needs boxed state, which is a normal runtime policy
    improvement rather than a workload-shaped optimization
- Verification:
  - focused raw-carrier + mono-array regression slice:
    - `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'Test(BytecodeRawIntegerResultValueUsesDirectUnsignedCarriers|BytecodeVM_CastOpcodeFastProducesRawU64FromRawU32|BytecodeVM_StoreSlotTypedExactRawIntegerPreservesRawU64|BytecodeVM_StoreSlotTypedExactLargeRawUnsignedIntegerStillUsesRawSlotCell|BytecodeVM_BinaryIntAddReturnsRawSmallU64Result|BytecodeVM_ArrayMemberFastPathMonoU32GetSkipsBoxedState|BytecodeVM_ArrayReadSlotMemberFastReadsMonoU32Handle|BytecodeVM_ArrayPushMemberFastAppendsMonoU32WithoutMaterializingState|BytecodeVM_ArrayWriteSlotFastPreservesMonoU32HandleWithoutMaterializingState|BytecodeVM_DirectArrayIndexSetPreservesMonoU32HandleWithoutMaterializingState|BytecodeVM_ExactNativeArrayReadFastReadsMonoU64WithoutMaterializingState|InterpreterMatchesTypeUsesMonoU32MetadataWithoutMaterializingArrayValues|InterpreterMatchesTypeEmptyMonoArrayStillMatchesUnknownElementTypeWithoutMaterializing|BytecodeStackSnapshotValueCopiesRawIntegerSlotCellAsRawValue)$' -count=1 -timeout 60s`
    - result: `ok able/interpreter-go/pkg/interpreter 0.067s`
  - bounded low-memory bytecode-runtime spot-checks:
    - `sum_u32_small`:
      - before handle-write invalidation keep:
        `3588503549 ns/op`, `263697664 B/op`, `19912280 allocs/op`
      - after:
        `3406593473 ns/op`, `167689984 B/op`, `21912107 allocs/op`
    - `word_count_small` control:
      - before:
        `1379663349 ns/op`, `96984336 B/op`, `1058389 allocs/op`
      - after:
        `1449628607 ns/op`, `96984192 B/op`, `1058383 allocs/op`
  - refreshed bounded `sum_u32_small` alloc-space profile:
    - before this keep, the leading shared alloc-space entries still included
      `runtime.u32ToValue(...)` (`85MB`) and
      `deoptTypedArrayToDynamic(...)` (`30.52MB flat`, `115.53MB cum`)
    - after this keep, both fell out of the top table entirely
    - the new top entry is now `bytecodeRawIntegerResultValue(...)`
      (`147.50MB flat`, `161.50MB cum`), which means the next remaining cost
      is shared raw-result allocation churn rather than typed-array state
      conversion
- Outcome:
  - kept
  - this removed a real general typed-array deopt boundary and cut
    `sum_u32_small` bytes/op materially without teaching the VM or compiler
    anything benchmark-specific
  - the alloc profile now says the runtime-array boundary is much cleaner;
    the dominant remaining cost has moved into raw unsigned result allocation

- Next target:
  - stay on the same general path and attack the new
    `bytecodeRawIntegerResultValue(...)` wall

    cast/binary/index-read paths where the VM is still allocating a fresh

    source after typed-array deopt removal

## 2026-06-30 — Reuse raw integer stack cells for generic unsigned cast/add/index results (v12)

- What changed:
  - updated
    [bytecode_vm_types.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_types.go),
    [bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value.go),
    and
    [bytecode_vm_integer_fast.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_integer_fast.go)
    so the VM now has a reusable per-stack-index raw integer lane for
    non-`i32` integer results, and raw integer casts route directly into that
    stack lane instead of manufacturing a fresh interface-backed raw result
    value first
  - refactored
    [bytecode_vm_ops.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_ops.go)
    so same-type small-int add/sub in the shared `execBinary(...)` path now
    reuse the new raw integer stack lane for every integer kind, not just the
    older dedicated `i32` / `i64` cases
  - updated
    [bytecode_vm_index_cache.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_index_cache.go)
    so direct mono `u32` / `u64` `Array` index reads used by
    `bytecodeOpArrayIndexGetSlot` append their results straight into reusable
    stack cells instead of going through `bytecodeRawIntegerResultValue(...)`
  - extended
    [bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_raw_integer_value_test.go)
    and
    [bytecode_vm_index_cache_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_index_cache_test.go)
    with focused coverage for:
    - large `u32 -> u64` casts reusing a raw integer stack cell
    - large `u64` add results reusing a raw integer stack cell
    - mono `u32` direct array index reads reusing the same raw stack cell
      across repeated executions
- Why this keep stayed generic:
  - it removes allocation churn from shared VM result placement rather than
    from any benchmark AST shape, named container, or fixed expression fusion
  - the new stack lane is type-agnostic across primitive integer kinds and is
    used by the existing cast/add/index machinery; no benchmark-only opcode or
    lowering rule was introduced
  - the change is specifically about where general raw integer results live
    inside the VM after they have already been computed, which is reusable
    across integer-heavy workloads
- Verification:
  - focused raw-carrier/index regression slice:
    - `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'Test(BytecodeVM_(CastOpcodeFastProducesRawU64FromRawU32|CastOpcodeFastUsesRawI64StackCellForSmallIntSource|CastOpcodeFastUsesReusableRawU64StackCellForLargeRawU32|CastOpcodeFastUsesReusableRawU8StackCellForSmallIntSource|BinaryIntAddUsesRawI64StackCellForResult|BinaryIntAddUsesReusableRawU64StackCellBeyondSmallCache|BinaryIntSubUsesRawI32CarrierForResult|BinaryIntSubUsesReusableRawI32StackCellBeyondStaticCache|ArrayIndexGetSlotFastPath|ArrayIndexGetSlotUsesI32RegisterIndex|ArrayIndexGetSlotMonoCharFastPath|ArrayIndexGetSlotMonoU32UsesReusableRawStackCell|ArrayMemberFastPathMonoU32GetSkipsBoxedState|ArrayReadSlotMemberFastReadsMonoU32Handle|ArrayPushMemberFastAppendsMonoU32WithoutMaterializingState|ArrayWriteSlotFastPreservesMonoU32HandleWithoutMaterializingState|DirectArrayIndexSetPreservesMonoU32HandleWithoutMaterializingState|ExactNativeArrayReadFastReadsMonoU64WithoutMaterializingState)|BytecodeRawIntegerResultValueUsesDirectUnsignedCarriers|InterpreterMatchesTypeUsesMonoU32MetadataWithoutMaterializingArrayValues|InterpreterMatchesTypeEmptyMonoArrayStillMatchesUnknownElementTypeWithoutMaterializing|BytecodeStackSnapshotValueCopiesRawIntegerSlotCellAsRawValue)$' -count=1 -timeout 60s`
    - result: `ok able/interpreter-go/pkg/interpreter 0.066s`
  - bounded low-memory bytecode-runtime spot-checks:
    - `sum_u32_small`:
      - before this keep:
        `3406593473 ns/op`, `167689984 B/op`, `21912107 allocs/op`
      - after:
        `2296764526 ns/op`, `15694784 B/op`, `1912743 allocs/op`
    - `word_count_small` control:
      - before:
        `1449628607 ns/op`, `96984192 B/op`, `1058383 allocs/op`
      - after:
        `1459012200 ns/op`, `96984016 B/op`, `1058374 allocs/op`
    - `nbody_small` non-unsigned numeric control:
      - after:
        `3865059112 ns/op`, `183097432 B/op`, `10115707 allocs/op`
  - refreshed bounded `sum_u32_small` alloc-space profile:
    - total sampled alloc space fell from about `208MB` to about `49.8MB`
    - `bytecodeRawIntegerResultValue(...)` is no longer a dominant flat
      allocation source; it now appears only as about `6.1MB` cumulative
      under remaining build-side immediate arithmetic
    - the new leading per-iteration runtime entries are
      `ArrayStoreAppendU32Promote(...)`, `bytecodeRawI32SlotCachedValue(...)`,
      and `bytecodeMultiplyIntegerImmediateFast(...)`
- Outcome:
  - kept
  - this removed the generic raw unsigned result-construction wall without
    specializing codegen or inventing benchmark-shaped bytecodes
  - the change materially improves `sum_u32_small` while leaving the text
    control effectively unchanged, which is the right shape for a reusable VM
    optimization
- Next target:
  - stay on the same generic path and target the remaining build-side integer
    immediate/update churn
  - this will entail profiling and tightening the shared `i32` immediate
    arithmetic / append path (`bytecodeMultiplyIntegerImmediateFast(...)`,

  - updated the generic `execBinarySlotConst(...)` operand read in

      - after:
        `2449604067 ns/op`, `8044200 B/op`, `123 allocs/op`
    - `word_count_small` control:
      - after:
        `1465767917 ns/op`, `96984080 B/op`, `1058377 allocs/op`
    - `random_lcg_i64_small` control:

  - refreshed bounded `sum_u32_small` alloc-space profile:

## 2026-07-01 — Reuse transient single-binding match/rescue clause envs conservatively (v12)

- Motivation:
  - shared match/rescue clause-scope environment churn only
  - no benchmark-shaped opcode, lowering rule, direct-call fusion, or
    nominal/container-specific specialization
  - bounded `word_count_small` allocation profiling had moved the dominant
    remaining reusable environment wall away from function-call generic
    binding setup and onto repeated clause-scope single-binding env creation
    in `matchPatternFastWithScopeReuse(...)`
- What changed:
  - added
    [environment_reuse.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/runtime/environment_reuse.go)
    plus
    [environment_shared_state.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/runtime/environment_shared_state.go)
    so transient env objects can be reset for one-binding reuse with:
    - parent/shared-state rebinding
    - binding/meta cleanup
    - monotonic environment revision bumps for bytecode cache invalidation
    - shared-state identity tracking for runtime-data cache safety
  - updated
    [runtime_data_cache.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/runtime_data_cache.go),
    [interpreter.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/interpreter.go),
    [bytecode_vm_types.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_types.go),
    and
    [bytecode_vm_pool.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_pool.go)
    so interpreter/VM runtime-data caches key off both revision and shared
    runtime-data state identity; this is what makes env-object reuse safe even
    when the same env object later hangs under a different parent chain with
    the same numeric revision
  - extended
    [scope_capacity.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/scope_capacity.go)
    and
    [match_clause_scope_cache.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/match_clause_scope_cache.go)
    with a conservative `transientSingleBindOK` clause plan bit
  - added
    [match_clause_env_reuse.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/match_clause_env_reuse.go)
    so simple identifier / typed-identifier clauses can acquire and release a
    transient env from a pool without changing any multi-binding or escaping
    pattern path
  - wired that helper through:
    - [eval_expressions_dispatch.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/eval_expressions_dispatch.go)
    - [bytecode_vm_controlflow.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_controlflow.go)

## 2026-07-01 — pool transient non-escaping call env shells for shared invocation paths (v12)

- Context:
  - after removing per-call generic constraint binding maps, the refreshed
    bounded `persistent_sorted_set_i32_small` profile still showed the next
    dominant shared wall in `invokeFunction(...)` line `localEnv =
    runtime.NewEnvironmentWithBindingSets(...)`
  - the remaining cost was not benchmark-specific dispatch logic; it was
    repeated environment-shell allocation for generic/runtime-binding calls
    that could not reuse the closure env and did not qualify for the older
    immutable reusable-env cache
- What changed:
  - extended
    [environment_reuse.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/runtime/environment_reuse.go)
    with `ResetForBindingSetsReuse(...)`, a general reset helper that clears a
    reused environment, rebinds parent/shared-state identity, drops stale
    runtime data / struct metadata, and reseeds up to two ordered binding sets
  - added
    [call_transient_env_reuse.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/call_transient_env_reuse.go)
    with:
    - a cached callable-shape check for whether a function/lambda body can
      produce an env-capturing value
    - a transient call-env pool that acquires/reseeds `Environment` shells via
      the new runtime reset helper
  - updated
    [eval_expressions_calls.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/eval_expressions_calls.go)
    so function/lambda invocation now uses that pooled transient env path
    whenever:
    - closure-env reuse is not legal
    - the older immutable reusable-bytecode-env cache does not apply
    - the callable body is conservatively non-escaping
  - kept the older immutable reusable env cache unchanged for the stronger
    no-mutation / slot-safe cases; this tranche broadens coverage by handling
    per-invocation mutable env shells safely, not by replacing the earlier
    cache
- Why this keep stayed generic:
  - eligibility depends only on shared semantic shape: whether a callable body
    can create env-capturing closures/iterators/spawns/placeholders/nested
    defs
  - it does not inspect benchmark names, stdlib types, or expression
    sequences, and it does not add any new bytecode form or lowering branch

    fresh-allocation path

- Context:

    runtime-lowered expression bodies such as match-clause branches
  - the first follow-up hypothesis was generic and plausible:
    allow `bytecodeOpStructLiteralNamedFast` to lower simple named struct

    runtime

    [bytecode_vm_struct_literal_fast.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_struct_literal_fast.go)
    so the runtime fast opcode can:
    - resolve its struct definition lazily
    - reuse the shared named-struct literal plan cache when compile-time field
      order is unavailable
    - handle zero-field singleton literals through the same fast opcode
  - updated
    [bytecode_lowering_struct_literals.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_lowering_struct_literals.go)
    and
    [struct_literal_named.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/struct_literal_named.go)
    so lowering can defer definition lookup safely for env-free singleton
    literals, while fielded env-free literals stay on the old generic
    `bytecodeOpStructLiteral` path
  - added focused coverage in
    [bytecode_vm_struct_literal_fast_test.go](/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/interpreters/go/pkg/interpreter/bytecode_vm_struct_literal_fast_test.go)
    for:
    - generic named-struct fast lowering in normal function bodies
    - env-free singleton literal lowering that defers runtime definition
      lookup
- Why the broad version was rejected:
  - the broad fielded variant did exactly what it was supposed to do
    structurally:
    bounded stats on `persistent_sorted_set_i32_small` moved generic
    `bytecodeOpStructLiteral` execution from about `56.1k` hits to `0`, with
    `bytecodeOpStructLiteralNamedFast` absorbing that traffic
  - but the bounded runtime tradeoff was wrong for the current VM:
    the same direct persistent-set sample moved from about
    `2.07s`, `38.09MB/op`, `483.8k allocs/op` to about
    `2.30-2.40s`, `31.6MB/op`, `284.3k allocs/op`
  - that means the broad keep reduced allocation churn materially but paid too
    much extra bytecode dispatch on field-expression evaluation inside those
    runtime-lowered expression programs
  - because the user goal is general runtime speed, not only lower allocation
    counts, that broader fielded keep was backed out instead of being recorded
    as progress
- Verification:
  - focused struct-literal slice:
    - `env GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_(StructLiteralNamedFastInFunctionBody|GenericStructLiteralNamedFastInFunctionBody|LowerExpressionSingletonStructLiteralFastWithoutEnvDefinition|ZeroFieldNamedStructLiteralReturnsDefinitionAndMatchesStructPattern)$' -count=1`
    - result: `ok`
  - bounded direct persistent-set check on the final narrowed tree:
    - `env GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 ABLE_BENCH_RUNTIME_TARGET=/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12/fixtures/bench/persistent_sorted_set_i32_small/main.able ABLE_BENCH_RUNTIME_RUN_FROM=/home/david/sync/projects/able/v12 /tmp/able-struct-fast.test -test.run '^$' -test.bench BenchmarkBytecodeProgramRuntime -test.benchmem -test.benchtime=1x`
    - result: about `2.36s`, `38.05MB/op`, `483.8k allocs/op`
  - bounded wrapper spot-check on the final narrowed tree:
    - `env GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 ./bench_perf --runs 1 --timeout 60 --modes bytecode-runtime fixtures/bench/persistent_sorted_set_i32_small/main.able`
    - result: `2068139673 ns/op`, `38058256 B/op`, `483770 allocs/op`
- Outcome:

## 2026-07-03 — broaden slot-lowered match coverage for named struct fields (v12)

- Context:
  - the previous rejected experiment showed that env-aware expression lowering
    removed fallback named struct literals inside nested match bodies but
    regressed wall time and bytes/op
  - the next generic target was therefore the existing slot-lowered match
    path: avoid nested match-body bytecode VMs for more real language patterns
    without adding benchmark-specific expression fusion
- What changed:
  - extended bytecode slot-match planning to cover simple named struct field
    patterns such as `TreeNode { value, left, right }` and renamed direct
    bindings such as `TreeNode { value::rv }`
  - kept the accepted subset conservative: named non-positional structs only,
    fields must resolve against the struct definition, and field subpatterns
    must be identifiers or wildcards; guards and nested/literal/typed field
    subpatterns still fall back to the generic matcher
  - allowed empty named struct patterns like `TreeEmpty {}` to use the existing
    typed-pattern jump path, while singleton struct identifier patterns still
    fall back to the generic matcher
  - added `bytecodeOpLoadSlotStructField`, a generic slot-framed struct-field
    read used by the new destructuring lowering instead of emitting a separate
    `LoadSlot` + `MemberAccess` pair for each field binding
  - fixed env-side match eligibility so visible singleton constructor
    identifiers are not misclassified as bindable slot patterns; this prevents
    slot-framed functions from containing generic match fallbacks whose nested
    expression evaluator cannot see slot-only parameters
- Verification:
  - focused match-slot tests:
    - `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestBytecodeVM_SlotLowering(EmitsZeroFieldNamedStructMatchWithoutGenericMatch|EmitsEmptyNamedStructMatchWithoutGenericMatch|EmitsNamedStructFieldPatternWithoutGenericMatch|SingletonIdentifierPatternFallsBackToGenericMatch)' -count=1`
    - result: `ok`
  - affected fixture parity:
    - `GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB GOGC=50 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/interpreter -run 'TestExecFixtureParity/04_06_01_union_payload_patterns|TestExecFixtures/04_06_01_union_payload_patterns' -count=1`
    - result: `ok`
  - full `go test ./pkg/interpreter` was also attempted under the same memory
    cap; it completed without OOM but still fails in unrelated pre-existing
    areas, so it is not a clean gate for this tranche
  - bounded `persistent_sorted_set_i32_small` bytecode samples after the change
    were approximately `2.00s/op`, `45.4MB/op`, `460.5k allocs/op`
- Outcome:
  - kept as a generic semantic/coverage improvement, but not counted as a
    performance win yet
  - compared with the prior control for this fixture (`~1.98s`,
    `36.1MB/op`, `433.5k allocs/op`), the broader lowering exposes extra
    allocation pressure that still needs to be removed before this path is a
    clear benchmark win
- Next target:
  - profile why slot-lowered named struct field matches increase allocations
    in the benchmark harness despite removing nested match-body evaluation
  - likely areas: per-function lowering allocations in larger slot programs,
    typed-pattern checks for generic union variants, and field-binding slot
    materialization
  - keep the work generic; do not add benchmark-specific match fusions or
    structure-name special cases

## 2026-07-08 guarded implicit local slots

- Scope:
  - stayed on generic bytecode VM/lowering mechanics for simple identifier
    assignment
  - did not touch the tree-walker, compiler/AOT lowering, stdlib source, named
    containers, helper-name fast paths, or benchmark-specific expression/source
    fusions

  - static opcode audit over `sum_u32_small`, `word_count_small`, and
    `linked_list_iterator_pipeline_i64_small` showed slot-framed functions
    still had static `LoadName` sites for locals introduced with typed `=`
  - examples included `values`, `total`, `counts`, and `builder`; this was a
    generic lowering gap because the v12 spec says `=` may implicitly declare a
    binding if no accessible binding exists
- Kept changes:
  - added guarded implicit-local bytecode slots for simple `=` assignment
    targets in slot-framed functions
  - first guarded store checks the runtime environment chain; if an outer
    binding exists it assigns that binding, otherwise it activates a frame slot
    for the current call
  - later guarded loads/stores use the slot only when the runtime decision made
    the name local
  - kept guarded slots separate from stable slots so existing specialized slot
    fast paths continue to apply only to statically stable bindings
  - added `LoadImplicitSlot`, `StoreImplicitSlot`, and
    `CompoundAssignImplicitSlot` as generic identifier-binding bytecodes
  - carried guarded-slot activation state through full, self-fast, and minimal
    self-fast call frames, returns, error unwinding, and VM pooling
  - added low-allocation raw-integer slot stack pushes so raw integer slot
    loads do not allocate boxed values in loops
  - refused guarded implicit slots for assignment to the current function's own
    name, preserving existing self-call disabling and `CallName` behavior
  - extended the opcode audit to count `LoadImplicitSlot` and
    `StoreImplicitSlot`

## 2026-07-13 - Bytecode i32 Frame ABI Feasibility Gate

- Scope:
  - audited the existing i32 register/value-slot paths, inline-call setup,
    call-frame save/restore, return completion, and bytecode slot analysis
  - evaluated the VM-v2 typed-frame direction without changing runtime code
- Finding:
  - current i32 registers and value-slot arrays are sidecars around
    `[]runtime.Value`; activation reads the value frame, inline calls build a
    value-frame callee, and returns still use `runtime.Value`
  - `i32RegisterFrame` is admitted by a syntactic AST traversal, not by the
    program typechecker's AST-node inference map
  - a narrow direct-call raw-cell or return change would therefore repeat the
    already rejected sidecar and micro-guard approaches rather than form a
    real typed ABI
- Decision:
  - keep no VM/compiler/runtime/stdlib change in this tranche
  - require a typechecker-backed, frame-owned primitive lane with explicit
    materialization at all dynamic/runtime boundaries before any i32 call or
    return ABI work is attempted
- Next:
  - carry successful module inference into production bytecode lowering and
    add conservative proof/fallback tests before changing frame storage
- Record:
  - `v12/design/bytecode-i32-frame-abi-gate.md`
